content: Fact Check: This video of a woman assaulting a Muslim man on a train is not a result of 'The Kashmir Files' ‘The Kashmir Files’, Vivek Agnihotri’s controversial film on the exodus of Kashmiri Hindus in the 90s, has reportedly led to incidents of hate speech against Muslims. Amid this, a video of a woman assaulting a Muslim man on a train has gone viral with the claim that this incident was a ramification of the film.Several people on Twitter and Facebook shared the video with captions like, “This is the current trend following the release of ‘The Kashmir Files’, Bharat Mata ki Jai. Jai Shree Ram.”advertisementALSO READ | Many lies projected in The Kashmir Files, says former J&K CM Omar AbdullahThe India Today Anti-Fake News War room (AFWA) found that this incident took place in October 2021 and has no connection with ‘The Kashmir Files’. The woman in the video is Madhu Sharma, a disciple of controversial preacher Yati Narsinghanand. She reportedly assaulted a Muslim man for pushing her while passing through the coach.ALSO READ | Exposed business of terrorism through my film 'The Kashmir Files': Vivek AgnihotriThe viral posts are achieved here, here and here.AFWA probeWith the help of a keywords search, we found a news report on The Wire containing photos that appeared to be screengrabs from the viral video.According to the report published on October 19, 2021, the woman seen in the viral video was Madhu Sharma, also known as Maa Madhura. Reportedly, she was a disciple of controversial religious leader Yati Narsinghanand. The woman reportedly assaulted a Muslim man on a train and “made him touch her feet for allegedly pushing her while passing through the railway coach gallery.”According to The Wire, Sharma shared the viral video on her Facebook page on October 18, 2021. She has since locked her profile.ALSO READ | Who wants Kashmir Files? KCR takes swipe at BJPThe same incident was also later reported by The Print and by another more online news portals in October 2021.We could not independently verify the details of the incident as reported by these news outlets. But it is clear that this incident, which was first reported in October 2021, had nothing to do with ‘The Kashmir Files’.
label: rumor

content: Fact Check: Simulated video of Ethiopian plane crash shared as final moments before Chinese Boeing 737 crash A passenger plane with over 130 people on board crashed on Monday afternoon, March 21, in a mountainous area of China. The Boeing 737 plane, operated by China Eastern Airlines, reportedly went down in Guangxi, an autonomous region in southern China.Even as casualties remained unknown at the time of writing this, a ten-second-long video allegedly from the ill-fated flight went viral on social media.advertisementThe video, which appears to be taken from the window of a plane, captured the sound of crying passengers. The first few seconds of the video showed the plane tumbling towards the ground. It crashed right before the ten-second mark.A Boeing 737 just crashed in southern China. This was one of the last moment recorded on the plane. maybe the only moment. Viewers’ discretion advised. pic.twitter.com/rzdRpNBEem — A Bass (@chanteur_sagi) March 21, 2022“A Boeing 737 just crashed in southern China. This was one of the last moments recorded on the plane. maybe the only moment. Viewers’ discretion advised,” a Twitter user wrote sharing the video.Archived versions of similar claims can be seen here and here.The India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) found this claim to be false. The viral video was a computer-generated simulation of another plane crash that took place nearly three years ago.AFWA ProbeAs per news reports, the Chinese plane crashed into a mountain. But in the viral video, we could barely see any mountainous terrain. In the comments under the video, many stated that the video was that of a crashing Ethiopian Airlines plane. Others suggested it was a simulated clip.Taking this as a cue, we looked for images of Ethiopian Airlines. We compared the logo of Ethiopian Airlines with the logo that appeared on the plane’s wing in the viral video and found them to be the same.So, does this video capture the final moments of an Ethiopian Airlines plane crash? No.We reverse-searched frames from the viral video, and it took us to a YouTube video uploaded to a channel called Bull Bosphorus on March 11, 2019.The video was a simulation of the Ethiopian Airlines crash that occurred on March 10, 2019. A Boeing 737 Max crashed and claimed the lives of 157 people.In the simulation, the viral clip appears at the 9:33 mark. It was clearly asserted in the description of the video: “This is not exactly what happened, this is only a simulated flight crash for Ethiopian Airlines flight ET302.”Therefore, it can be concluded that the simulated video of the 2019 Ethiopian crash was falsely shared as the recent crash in Southern China.
label: truth

content: Fact Check: Rahul Gandhi mocked on Society media with clipped video from 2020   A video of Rahul Gandhi has been doing rounds on social media in which, he can be heard saying, “Not only in Hindustan, the Indian youth can bring change to the entire nation.”Several social media users shared the video, mocking Rahul Gandhi.The India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) found that the viral video was clipped. In the original video, the Congress leader corrected himself within moments of this faux pas.advertisementArchived versions of posts with similar claims can be seen here and here.AFWA PROBEWhile investigating the claim, we first noticed that the podium in front of Gandhi mentioned the words “Yuva Aakrosh Rally” and the date “January 28”.Taking this as a cue, we conducted a keyword search and found the original video uploaded to YouTube on January 28, 2020. Caption with this video reads, “Shri Rahul Gandhi addresses Yuva Aakrosh Rally in Jaipur, Rajasthan.”At the 2:35 minutes mark in this video Rahul Gandhi could be seen making the statement given in the viral video.In the original video, Gandhi first stated, “Not only in Hindustan, but the Indian youth can also bring change to the entire nation.” However, he immediately corrected himself and said, “Not only in India, but the Indian youth can also bring changes to the whole world.”Hence, we can conclude that the claim with this video is misleading. The viral video is a clipped version of the original video. In the original video, Gandhi corrected his mistake immediately after saying it.
label: truth

content: Fact Check: No, Malaysia hasn't agreed to hand over Zakir Naik to India Several social media users recently claimed that controversial Islamic televangelist and preacher Zakir Naik is being extradited to India from Malaysia. The claim, shared along with the footage of a news report by ABP Live, hailed the Narendra Modi-led government for this."Zakir Naik being brought back to India another achievement by MODI govt.. burnol stocks for liberals needed," one such tweet said.advertisementSimilar claims have been archived here and here.The India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) has found the claim misleading. The news clip shared was from 2018.AFWA ProbeNaik is wanted in India for hate speech, money laundering, and terror-related activities. We first looked for recent news reports on Naik. We set the Google custom time range to just the past month in our search. However, there were no reports by any mainstream news outlet.Since the video circulated along with the claim belonged to ABP Live, we checked the channel's Facebook page next. When we searched with his name, we found the news report in question was uploaded to the page on July 4, 2018.We ran a keyword search with a time range set to 2018. This led us to a report by Alt News from 2021 that debunked a similar claim about Zakir Naik's extradition. We found that the picture of Naik and the logo of a Facebook page on the video fact-checked by Alt News was the same as those on the videos shared now. The source of this video was a Facebook page called “Phir Ek Bar Modi Sarkar”.Hence, it became clear that the video was not new at all.We also found several news reports of then-Malaysian PM Mahathir Mohamad rejecting Naik's deportation to India. "As long as he is not creating any problem, we will not deport him because he has been given permanent residency status," the leader said at the time.These reports stated that India tried to get Naik from Malaysia via the extradition treaty between the two countries.On July 6, ABP Live also published a similar report that confirmed Malaysia's unwillingness to hand over Naik to India. This story can be read here.There was also a 2019 report in the Economic Times that said Mahathir denied PM Modi asking for Naik's extradition. He said that Modi made no extradition request when they met at Russia's Vladivostok during an economic forum.Thus, it can be safely concluded that India has not recently engaged Malaysia over the extradition of Zakir Naik. The news footage shared by several users is from 2018.(With inputs from Yash Mittal in New Delhi)
label: rumor

content: Fact Check: No, Bhagwant Mann isn't the youngest Chief Minister in Punjab's history Social media is abuzz with posts of appreciation and wishes for the new AAP government in Punjab. The new chief minister, Bhagwant Mann, was sworn-in on March 16, Wednesday, at Bhagat Singh's ancestral village, Khatkar Kalan.Among these were posts that congratulated the AAP leader on becoming the youngest Chief Minister of Punjab. "Bhagwant Singh Mann has been elected the 28th Chief Minister of Punjab. He's also been honoured as the youngest CM of Punjab, by becoming the CM at the age of 48," one such poster in Punjabi read.advertisementThe India Today Anti Fake News War Room has found that the claim is misleading. The record of being the youngest chief minister of Punjab is held by Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) patriarch Parkash Singh Badal. When sworn in as the chief minister in 1970, Senior Badal was 43 years old.AFWA ProbeWhile checking, we learned that Bhagwant Mann is actually 48 years old, as claimed in the post. He was born on October 17, 1973. However, there were no reports in the mainstream media that called him the youngest chief minister of Punjab. This was a major hint that the claim could be inaccurate, as it is unlikely for news organisations to skip such feats. No official handles of the AAP claimed to have given Punjab the youngest CM ever.We looked up the list of chief ministers of Punjab, which showed that senior SAD leader Parkash Singh Badal had held the office at the age of 43.Using Google keyword search, we retrieved more information on the topic. Following 94-year-old Parkash Badal's defeat from his bastion of Lambi in the 2022 Assembly polls, several national dailies pointed out his unique achievement of being chief minister at age 43. Given below are news reports that name the nonagenarian as the youngest CM in the state.Born on December 8, 1927, Senior Badal became a legislator for the first time in 1957. The five-time CM's first tenure in office was from 1970 to 1971-- when he was 43 years old."From 1970-71, Badal became the youngest chief minister of an Indian state. He first became chief minister of Punjab in March 1970 and headed a coalition government of Akali Dal [Sant] and Jana Sangh," an India Today article published on the leader's 89th birthday said.We further confirmed the information on the official website of SAD. "He has been the chief minister of the state from 1970 to 1971, from 1977 to 1980, from 1997 to 2002, and from 2007 to 2017 [two consecutive terms]... In 1970, he became the youngest chief minister of an Indian state," his profile on the party website read.Hence, it can be concluded that AAP's Bhagwant Mann isn't the youngest chief minister in the history of Punjab. The unique record is held by Parkash Singh Badal.(With inputs from Yash Mittal in New Delhi)
label: truth

content: Fact Check: These minors thrashed by UP police in Chandauli was not due to sloganeering for Pakistan A disturbing video of police atrocities against two people has gone viral with the claim that UP policemen are thrashing them for shouting slogans in favour of Pakistan.Multiple Twitter and Facebook users have posted this viral clip along with the Hindi caption that reads, “UP police is teaching them a lesson for shouting slogans in favour of Pakistan”.India Today Anti-Fake News War room ( AFWA) has found that the viral video is related to an incident that took place in Chandauli in 2021. Two cops of UP Police were suspended for thrashing two minors over the allegations of theft.advertisementThe 2021 incident has no connection to any pro-Pakistan sloganeering.AFWA probeWith the help of keywords search, India Today found a couple of news reports along with the same video or the screen grab of the viral video. The Hindi news portal “Amar Ujala”, used a screengrab of the same viral video and published a news report on May 2, 2021.As per the news report, this incident took place in Balua Police station area of UP’s Chandauli district. Following an allegation of a theft in a mobile store in that area, the local police chowki in-charge Shivanand Verma and constable Dilip Kumar reached the spot and brutally thrashed two suspects. The video of the police atrocities was caught on camera and went viral.According to the Chandauli police, the two personnel were suspended after a departmental inquiry.The Chandrauli Police refuted the claim that the incident was linked to pro-Pakistan sloganeering, as had been claimed by social media users.The Times of India had reported the same incident along with the viral video on May 6, 2021. The headline of the video story reads, “ UP: Cops brutally beat up minors over mobile theft allegation, video goes viral”Thus, it is confirmed that an old incident related to theft and police atrocities against minors has gone viral with a communal twist.
label: rumor

content: Fact Check: This is not Russia preparing mass graves for its soldiers killed in Ukraine war More than 150,000 troops are deployed by Russia as part of its war efforts in Ukraine. As per the American intelligence estimates, the invasion army has already lost over 7,000 personnel since the start of the war.Amid this revelation by the media, a video of long rows of dug graves is circulated on social media with the claim that it was prepared by the Russian government for their soldiers brought dead from Ukraine.advertisementOne such post on Facebook that received over 270K views until the time of filing this story can be seen below.India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) has found that the claim along with the video is misleading. This video has been on the internet at least since 2021. According to Russian authorities, it showed a common practice in the northern cities of Russia where graves are dug ahead of the winter.AFWA probeWe did a reverse search of the keyframes of the viral video and found the same video shared by Russian social media handles at least since October 2021. This confirmed that the video is old and not related to the Russia-Ukraine war that started in February 2022.Some netizens who posted the video in 2021 also claimed that the video is from Russia’s Surgut.Using online tools Live Transcribe and Google Translator we translated the audio component of the video shared in 2021. According to the audio, the graves were prepared in a city cemetery in Surgut "ahead of the fourth wave of Covid-19."However, we found some other responses to the video which stated that the winter in Surgut is harsh and hence the graves are dug in advance as a common practice.We further checked the Instagram handle of Surgut Mayor Andrey Filatov and found the same video of mass graves in question posted by him on March 7, 2022.In his clarification note, Filatov stated that the video was from 2021 and it showed graves being dug ahead of winter in Surgut. He added that such practices were common for at least a decade and a half in northern cities of Russia where winter is extreme.The clarification was posted along with the clipping from an interview provided by him to a channel regarding the video.The explanation provided by the Mayor in the Russian language was loosely translated as, “For several days now, a fake video has been circulating on the Internet claiming that the Surgut cemetery is being prepared to receive the soldiers who died during the special operation. I declare unequivocally that this information is false. The video is indeed from our cemetery, but the footage is from last year. We already commented on them in September 2021. At that time, the graves were being prepared for winter. This is a standard procedure for earthworks in northern cities. Due to the fact that we have rather low temperatures in winter, all work of this specific nature is carried out in advance. This has been practised for at least 15 years.”Multiple Russian news portals have also published this clarification provided by the Mayor of Surgut. The reports also confirms that in winter the ground in this region freezes, making it difficult to dig graves.It is hence clear that the video in question is old and not related to the ongoing war between Russia and Ukraine.
label: truth

content: Old incident of diplomat’s arrest in Ukraine for smuggling revived amid ongoing war A photo of a box full of currency notes has gone viral on social media with the claim that Ukrainian authorities arrested a diplomat who was trying to smuggle money and gold from the country.Several Twitter users shared the image with captions like: “The Ukrainian Investigative Bureau has arrested a Ukrainian diplomat while he was trying to smuggle $140,000, 68,000 euros, 12 kilograms of gold bars and 13.8 kilograms of gold jewellery.”advertisementThe India Today Anti-Fake News War room ( AFWA) found that the claimed arrest and seizure by Ukrainian authorities actually took place in February 2021 near the Ukraine-Poland border.The viral posts are archived here and here.AFWA PROBEWith the help of a keywords search, we came across a Ukrainian news report titled, “The DBR will transfer $1 million of the seized funds to the Armed Forces”.As per the report, the State Bureau of Investigation (DBR) had confiscated about $1 million worth of gold and foreign currency, and valuables from a Ukrainian embassy employee in the EU last year.“At the Yahodyn checkpoint on February 28, 2021, during a search of a diplomatic minibus, DBR investigators found and seized almost 68,000, more than $140,000, more than 12 kg of gold bars, and gold jewellery weighing 13.8 kg,” the report said.Taking this as a clue, we looked up the website and the social media accounts of Ukraine's State Bureau of Investigation (DBR).The DBR announced a donation of $1 million to the Ukrainian government for the army’s needs on March 17.The Facebook page of the DBR also shared details about this donation. It confirmed that the DBR had seized gold and currency worth about $1 million from one of the employees of the Ukrainian Embassy in the EU who attempted to illegally take them abroad. Now “these funds are transferred to the state budget and can be used for the needs of the Armed Forces of Ukraine,” a post on the DBR’s Facebook page read.“At the checkpoint of Yagodin of the Volyn Customs Service on February 28, last year, investigators of the DBR conducted an inspection of a diplomatic minibus, in which almost 68 thousand euros, over 140 thousand US dollars, over 12 kilograms of gold bars and gold jewellery with a total weight of 13.8 kg, and a lot of cigarettes were seized,” a rough translation of the post said.This seizure was a joint operation conducted by the Security Service of Ukraine (SSU) and the DBR. Both the SSU’s and the DBR’s Twitter accounts had posted about this operation on March 1, 2021.advertisementThe verified YouTube channel of the SSU had shared a video of the seizure on March 1, 2021. The details given in the YouTube video were the same that shared by the DBR in their press note recently about the donation.The same incident was also reported by international news agencies last year.Thus, it is clear that an old incident of an arrest of a diplomat was falsely claimed to be recent.
label: truth

content: Fact Check: Here’s why viral RTI reply says only 89 Kashmiri Pandits were killed by militants in J&K Vivek Agnihotri’s new film, ‘The Kashmir Files’, has brought the killings and the exodus of Kashmiri Pandits in the late 80s and the early 90s into the mainstream and discussions around it have dominated social media since its release.Amid the discussion, an image of an RTI response has gone viral on social media with the claim that only 89 Kashmiri Pandits were killed by militants in Jammu and Kashmir.advertisementWhile this figure has been quoted by many, some raised doubts on social media about its authenticity, asking if the figure accounted for Kashmiri Pandits killed in Srinagar alone or in the whole of Jammu and Kashmir.Several Facebook users shared the photo of the viral RTI response with captions like, “Kashmir Police replies in the RTI on Kashmiri Pandits' killing. Total Pandits killed = 89, Total other faiths killed = 1635.”The India Today Anti-Fake News War Room ( AFWA) found that the RTI response provided the death toll since 1990 and did not include killings in 1989.The viral posts are archived here, here and here.What did the RTI reply say?Last year, RTI activist PP Kapoor from Haryana’s Samalkha (Panipat), raised multiple queries in his RTI application regarding the rehabilitation and migration of Kashmiri Pandits and others in the valley. One of the queries asked for the “number of Kashmiri Pandits who were killed by terrorist attacks”.The DSP of the district police headquarters in Srinagar informed in the RTI reply on November 27, 2021, that number of “Kashmiri Pandits who were killed by terrorist attacks since the inception of militancy 1990 = 89”.It is to be noted that the RTI activist did not ask about the number of deaths of Kashmiri Pandits starting from a particular year. In the reply, the J&K police provided figures only from 1990 and excluded the year 1989.AFWA got in touch with Kapoor over the phone, who has confirmed that the figure quoted in the RTI reply projected the number of Kashmiri Pandits killed in the entire state and not of Srinagar alone unlike as perceived by several netizens.How many Kashmiri Pandits were killed by militants?As per news reports which quoted the J&K police and the state government, over 200 Kashmiri Pandits have been killed due to militancy since 1989.As per a report published in The Indian Express in 2008, “Jammu and Kashmir Police report says that 209 Kashmiri Pandits were killed by militants since 1989.”According to this report, “of the 209 Kashmiri Pandits killed, 109 died in 1990.” That means that over 100 people were killed in 1989 alone — something that was not covered in the 2021 RTI response.A 2010 report from journalist Shujaat Bukhari in The Hindu quoted data provided by the Jammu and Kashmir government that said 219 Kashmiri Pandits had been killed by militants since 1989. Replying to a question from People's Democratic Party member Syed Basharat Bukhari, then Revenue Minister Raman Bhalla told the Assembly in Jammu that “219 Pandits were killed in Kashmir from 1989 to 2004.”Shujaat Bukhari, who wrote the aforementioned report, was shot dead by unidentified gunmen in Srinagar in 2018.Thus, it is clear that the wide gap in the number of Kashmiri Pandits killed as per news reports and as per the RTI response is different because of the base years that have been taken into account in each. That's why the death toll appears low in the RTI reply that has gone viral.
label: truth

content: Fact Check: No, Centre is NOT offering interest-free loans under KCC scheme from April 1 A screengrab from a newspaper has been going viral that states that from April 1, the Centre will offer loans at zero per cent under the Kisan Credit Card (KCC) scheme.The screengrab was shared along with captions that expressed gratitude to Prime Minister Narendra Modi. One such post’s caption said in Hindi: “Honourable Prime Minister, we are grateful to you.”advertisementThe India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) found the claim to be misleading. No such announcement has been made by the union government.Archived versions of posts with similar claims can be seen here and here.AFWA PROBEWhile investigating the claim, we first conducted a keyword search to find out whether the government had made any such announcements recently. We did not find a single news report or government press release that stated the government was offering an interest-free loan under the KCC scheme.To understand the present interest structure of loans under the KCC scheme, we visited the website of the State Bank of India.The SBI website stated that farmers could avail loans up to Rs 3 lakhs under the KCC scheme at an interest of seven per cent if the union government gave a subsidy of two per cent per annum on it. This meant that the actual interest rate was nine per cent per annum. The website was last updated on March 11, 2022, at the time of writing this.According to news reports, under the KCC scheme, farmers could avail loans up to Rs. 3 lakhs in five years for an interest rate of only four per cent per annum.However, for this to apply, farmers needed to repay their existing loans on time. If the farmer repaid the initial loan on time, he could get a rebate of three per cent. In this case, the farmer would need to pay interest at the rate of four per cent per annum only.To further confirm the claim, we got in touch with an SBI spokesperson. “No, we have not received any such circular yet that states loans under KCC would be interest-free from April 1, 2022,” the SBI spokesperson told India Today.Hence, we can conclude that the claim of this post is misleading. The union government has not made any announcement on providing interest-free loans under the KCC scheme.(With inputs from Sanjana Saxena in Lucknow)
label: rumor
