content: No, this video doesn't show US army troops paradropping into Ukraine during ongoing war  Recently, US President Joe Biden moved 12,000 troops along the borders with Russia, such as Latvia, Estonia, Lithuania, and Romania, vowing to “defend every inch of NATO territory — every single inch.”Despite the White House's refusal to make a military intervention in Ukraine, a video has gone viral on social media featuring soldiers being paradropped from a Globemaster III aircraft. Several posts on social media claim this video shows US soldiers landing in Ukraine. One such post can be seen here.advertisementThe India Today Anti-Fake News War room (AFWA) found the claim to be false. This video is from 2016 and shows the Airborne units of the US military making a static line jump. It is unrelated to the ongoing Russia-Ukraine war.AFWA ProbeFirst, we checked if the US had announced a military intervention in Ukraine. Using advanced search on Google, we filtered out the latest developments on the subject. However, there were no such news reports.A reverse search of the viral video's keyframes gave several results. This included articles on a YouTube video released in 2016 about the mobile game Pokemon GO. The video was released by animator Nicholas King aka 'Nickels', who combined CGI with original footage of paratroopers to create a dark comedy about how common Pokemons were distributed. We identified that the frame in which the Pokemons are loaded on the aircraft looked similar to a scene in the viral video. The background of both these frames looked the same.The video was uploaded on Nickel's YouTube channel on August 8, 2016.We also found a webpage called 'Wordless Tech' that had a similar photo. The page was titled 'Paratroopers Static Line Jump'. Published on July 28, 2016, the image was a screenshot from the video in which soldiers boarded the plane."Watch those paratroopers performing static line jumps from C-17 Globemaster III aircraft. They are from the 82nd and 101st Airborne Division, jumping over Sicily Drop Zone at Fort Bragg, North Carolina," the webpage read.Pursing this clue, we looked up Fort Bragg military installation on Google Maps. Using 3D satellite and Street View options, we discovered that the buildings and lamb poles of Fort Bragg's Pope Army Airfield looked similar to the ones in the video.The Wordless Tech page also had a link to a YouTube page. This took us to a longer version of the video that went viral as the American intervention in the Russia-Ukraine war. The verified page of AiirSource Military, which has 39.7 lakh subscribers, uploaded the video on May 28, 2016.The description of the video was the same as the one found on Wordless Tech.advertisementHence, we concluded that this video had nothing to do with the Russia-Ukraine war — it was almost six years old.
label: truth

content: Fact Check: This Ugandan cop was NOT attacking reporters with a catapult for asking irrelevant questions An image of a man in a police uniform aiming a slingshot has gone viral with the claim that this was the Uganda police spokesperson hitting a reporter for asking "irrelevant questions."Many on Facebook and Twitter shared this image with the caption, "Newly appointed Uganda police spokesperson hit a reporter with a catapult for asking irrelevant questions."The India Today Anti-Fake News War room ( AFWA) found that this claim was false. In 2021, Ugandan policemen seized a shipment of catapults. During the ensuing press conference, Fred Enanga, a police spokesperson, demonstrated how they were used.advertisementThe viral posts are archived here and here.AFWA probeWith the help of a keyword search, we found the original video of the Uganda police press conference uploaded to the YouTube channel of UBC Television Uganda on April 13, 2021. As per the details given alongside, Uganda cops were investigating a criminal gang that was allegedly "trading terror activities using catapults to destabilize the country."While addressing the media during a weekly brief, a police spokesperson, Fred Enanga, said suspects were apprehended in the matter and the police were trying to look for the rest of the gang members.In the YouTube video, we can see the police officers demonstrating to the reporters present during the media briefing the capabilities of the slingshots.This incident was reported by several news outlets in 2021.Enanga, during the briefing, said that the catapults or slingshots were “capable of firing metallic projectiles or bearings,” which made them deadly, “once possessed and used by the wrong elements.”Thus, we can conclude that the viral posts falsely claimed the policeman was attacking reporters for supposedly asking irrelevant questions.(With input from Yash Mittal)
label: rumor

content: Fact Check: No, this video does not show LK Advani breaking down after watching ‘The Kashmir Files’ Discussions on Vivek Agnihotri's new film 'The Kashmir Files', which tackles the exodus of Kashmiri Hindus in the 1990s and insurgency in the state, has dominated social media in the last few days.Amid praise and criticism of the film, a video went viral with the claim that it showed veteran Bharatiya Janata Party leader LK Advani at a movie theatre, overcome with emotion after watching the film.advertisementBJP leader Manish Grover, among others, shared the video with the aforementioned claim on his verified Facebook page.The archived versions of similar posts can be seen here, here and here.The India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) found that the claim along with the video was misleading. This video is from the screening of the movie 'Shikara' in 2020.AFWA probeWe noticed that many social media users pointed out the video in circulation was old. With the help of a keyword search, we found the same video and screenshots from it carried by several news reports in 2020. As per the reports, the video of Advani breaking down is from the screening of the Vidhu Vinod Chopra-directed film ‘Shikara’. This movie was based on the exodus of Kashmiri Hindus in the 90s as well.The video was also tweeted by Chopra himself in February 2020. “Shri LK Advani at the special screening of #Shikara. We are so humbled and grateful for your blessings and your appreciation for the film Sir,” the director wrote while sharing the video.Shri L K Advani at the special screening of #Shikara We are so humbled and grateful for your blessings and your appreciation for the film Sir. @foxstarhindi @rahulpandita pic.twitter.com/oUeymMayhc — Vidhu Vinod Chopra Films (@VVCFilms) February 7, 2020In a February 2020 interview, Chopra also spoke about his relationship with Advani and how the BJP leader had helped him financially in the early years of his career. He said that this was the reason he sent Advani a special invitation for the special screening of ‘Shikara’.Moreover, we couldn’t find any credible report about Advani attending the screening of ‘The Kashmir Files’. The official Twitter handle of Vivek Agnihotri has no mention of the veteran leader attending the film’s screening.With the available information, it is clear that the video of Advani breaking down at the movie theatre is from the screening of ‘Shikara’, and not related to ‘The Kashmir Files’.(With inputs from Anil Kumar in New Delhi)
label: truth

content: Fact Check: 2019 news clip from Haryana goes viral as proof of BJP capturing booths during UP polls Allegations of booth-capturing and EVM-rigging continue to spread on social media following the sweeping electoral victory of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) in Uttar Pradesh.A video of a news clip went viral along with the claim that voters were influenced by the BJP’s polling agents in booths in UP.The clip featured a reporter talking to a group of women who complained that a polling agent named Giriraj forced them to press the button with the BJP’s Lotus symbol.advertisementSir, This is what u are talking about, #BOOTH capturingDear PM Modi, This is how u win your electionAnd the EC knows this& deliberately sitting silent & giving winning certificate to BJP@realumeshsingh@RoopeshSinghINC@RobbieK014 @ashharwarsi_inc @IYCLegalCell @MaryDenniz pic.twitter.com/WoRYNrASd1 — Darryl (@Trendsetting123) March 12, 2022The captions of such viral posts said things like, “Now don't say that the secret of BJP's victory is the blessings of the people,” or “ Sir, This is what u are talking about, #BOOTH capturing. Dear PM Modi, This is how u win your election And the EC knows this & deliberately sitting silent & giving winning certificate to BJP.”The India Today Anti-Fake news War room ( AFWA) found that the viral news clip was from the 2019 Lok Sabha elections. In the original report, voters alleged booth-capturing in Faridabad, Haryana.The archived viral posts can be seen here and here.AFWA probeThe location mentioned in the viral NDTV news clip was Faridabad, Haryana. This made it clear that the video was not related to the 2022 Uttar Pradesh assembly polls.We found the original news clip on the YouTube channel of NDTV India, uploaded on May 13, 2019. The video was titled, "The Election Commission took action after the Faridabad video of booth-capturing went viral."In the original video, a reporter spoke to a group of women who alleged that a person named Giriraj forced them to cast their votes in favour of the BJP. A minute into the YouTube video, the viral portion of the news clip was seen.We took this as a clue and looked for news reports regarding the allegations from that time. We found several news reports from 2019. As per the reports, after a video of a person influencing voters at a booth in Palwal, Haryana went viral during the 2019 Lok Sabha polls, the Election Commission ordered re-polling. The person named Giriraj mentioned in the viral video was also arrested.Thus, it is clear that this video that went viral with allegations of booth-capturing in UP is not from the state at all. Nor is it from any of the recently-concluded assembly polls. It’s from 2019.(With input from Yash Mittal)
label: truth

content: Fact Check: No, Bengal government is not paying GST for Muslim traders A few days after West Bengal minister Chandrima Bhattacharya was handed over the key responsibility of the finance department, she presented her debut budget at the state assembly on Friday, March 11. Meanwhile, a screenshot has gone viral on social media claiming that the West Bengal government has waived off the GST for the Muslim traders of the state.Social media users on Facebook and Twitter have shared a Hindi screenshot that read, “GST waived off for the Muslim traders. Mamata government will pay their GST.”advertisementThe text further read, “Mamata Banerjee-led government of West Bengal has made a big decision. According to the Mamata government, the trade of Muslims was hurt by the introduction of the GST. That is why her government will pay all the due taxes of the Muslim businessmen. This means their taxes have been waived. The population of the Muslim community in Bengal has reached 35%. In such a situation, control of forming or dissolving any government is in their hands. This particular decision of the Mamata-led government proves that Bengal has indeed become an Islamic state.”Archived versions of the posts can be seen here and here.India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) has found that the screenshot's content is not at all true. The West Bengal government has neither taken nor announced any such decision.AFWA PROBEWith the help of a few relevant keywords, we tried to find any reports regarding the same. But there were no media reports that supported the claim. It is unlikely that such a major decision by the state government would go unreported by news outlets.Further search led us to some 4-year-old social media posts that made the same claim. A Twitter user had posted a cut-out of a Hindi newspaper on July 14, 2018. The headline of the story read, “The state government of West Bengal will now pay the taxes of Muslim traders.”The report revealed that the then finance minister of the state, Amit Mitra, had announced some support to the traders to file GST. Thus, we ran some more keywords to know the exact quote made by Amit Mitra on the matter. But again, there was no story available regarding this.Another striking factor in the story was a spelling mistake in its headline. The Hindi spelling of “businessmen” is wrong in the headline, which usually doesn't happen with mainstream newspapers.We reached out to West Bengal’s Minister of State for minority affairs, Ghulam Rabbani, who dismissed the claim. “These are rumours which have been spread by the opposition to defame our chief minister. Our party chief has always condemned the way GST was implemented. But claims like waving of GST from the Muslims doesn't make any sense,” he said.advertisementThus, it becomes evident that the West Bengal government has not made any decision to waive off the GST of the Muslim traders. Although it is true that Mamata Banerjee (http://bitly.ws/show/pgUC) has often been accused by the opposition parties of doing Muslim appeasement politics in the state.(With inputs from Yash Mittal, New Delhi)
label: rumor

content: Fact Check: Old photo from UK shared claiming BJP's victory in Uttar Pradesh featured at NYSE BJP's scintillating victory in four state assembly elections including Uttar Pradesh has thrilled party supporters. The waves of celebration by pro-BJP handles on social media are yet to die down. Among the posts that were shared by them include an image allegedly from the New York Stock Exchange with a digital scroll that showed the news of the BJP's win "in India's biggest state."advertisement"Just ZOOM and see at New York Stock exchange what is displayed in digital display," the photo was captioned by a user on Facebook.Similar posts have been archived here and here.The India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) has found this claim to be not true. The building in the picture is not the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE). The image was found online after the UP assembly elections in 2017.AFWA PROBEWe ran a keyword search on Google to find reports of assembly elections in India being displayed at the NYSE. But there were none."Modi wins landslide election victory in India's biggest state," the news scroll on the building read. When the line was Googled, a news report by Reuters was found. The photo story (https://reut.rs/3KKnvIl) was published on March 11, 2017. It was on this day Yogi Adityanath led BJP government retained power in Uttar Pradesh for the second time.A reverse image search of the viral photo was conducted. This led us to tweets by BJP IT wing in-charge Amit Malviya and Rajya Sabha MP Om Prakash Mathur. Both leaders had tweeted the viral photo from their verified handles on March 12, 2017.News of BJP's big win under Prime Minister Modi splashed in Canary Warf, prominent business district of London. Zoom it.. #IAmNewIndia pic.twitter.com/Z17OtsUatL — Amit Malviya (@amitmalviya) March 12, 2017This confirmed that the viral image is old.We noticed that Amit Malviya had claimed the spot of the photograph in his tweet. He identified the place as "Canary Warf, prominent business district of London," and not the New York Stock Exchange.With the help of Google Maps, we verified the premises of both places in question. While the exterior images of the Thomson Reuters building in Canary Wharf looked very similar to the photo, the area around NYSE looked different. Neither could we find any photos of a news screen at the front side of the NYSE building.In the viral photo, the news was displayed in a single-line digital news scroll with orange text. The same was found on the Thomson Reuters building.This concluded that the photo was not taken in the United States as claimed in the post.Hence, it can be concluded that the image shared following the BJP's victory in the assembly polls to Uttar Pradesh is old. The image seen in the photograph is not the New York Stock Exchange as claimed.(With inputs from Sanjana Saxena in Lucknow)
label: truth

content: Fact Check Video: No, Rahul didn't play badminton after poll drubbing A video of Congress leader Rahul Gandhi playing shuttle badminton has gone viral on social media along with the claim that he was seen playing amidst the party's heavy defeat in Assembly elections."After Congress faced humiliation in the five states, Rahul Gandhi was seen playing badminton", quoted a Hindi Facebook page named "Best Hindi News" while sharing this video.India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) has found this claim to be not true.
label: truth

content: Fact Check: No, Rahul Gandhi didn’t play badminton post Congress defeat in recent Assembly polls Indian National Congress has yet again tasted disappointment in the recent assembly elections in five states. The grand old party received a major setback even in Punjab -- a state where it was in power. Meanwhile, a video of the former party President Rahul Gandhi playing shuttle badminton has gone viral on social media along with the claim that he was seen playing amidst the party's heavy defeat.advertisementIn the video, Rahul can be seen playing badminton in an indoor court surrounded by a few party leaders, police, and security guards. Rahul's shots are applauded by the crowd in the video."After Congress faced humiliation in the five states, Rahul Gandhi was seen playing badminton", quoted a Hindi Facebook page named "Best Hindi News" while sharing this video.The official Facebook page of 'Punjab Kesari Madhya Pradesh/Chattisgarh' also posted the same video alongside a caption in Hindi that reads, "Rahul Gandhi was seen in a bit relaxed mood after the result of the 5 state assembly elections was declared. The video has gone viral."Archived versions of these claims can be seen here and here.India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) has found this claim to be not true. Rahul didn't play badminton after the results were announced. This video was shot in Kerala a day before the counting on March 10.AFWA ProbeWith the help of a few relevant keywords, we came across an article published by ABP News. The news report's cover image was a collage of two images of the Congress leader. While Rahul was photographed enjoying ice cream in one, he was holding a badminton racket in the other.Although the report was published on 10 March 2022, the headline clearly mentioned that the said activities were done by Rahul in Kerala before the poll results were announced.Further search led us to a YouTube video published by the official channel of Rahul Gandhi on March 9 -- a day before the poll results were declared.The description of this video explained that he enjoyed a game of badminton at the new indoor stadium at Sullamussalam Arts and Science College Areekode, Ernad, Malappuram.The official YouTube page of the Indian National Congress also uploaded the same video on March 9.Thus, it is clear that the video of Rahul Gandhi playing badminton was shot a day before the election results were declared on March 10.
label: truth

content: Fact Check: Video of bulldozer stunt does not show Yogi's victory celebration in UP As the BJP’s victory in UP became apparent on March 10, a short video clip of a bulldozer stunt began making the rounds on Twitter and Facebook with the claim that this was how people were celebrating Yogi Adityanath’s victory.The caption in Hindi on one such viral post reads, “Long live, Bulldozer Baba. There is no limit to the happiness of bulldozers in UP today.”
label: truth

content: Fact Check: Old photos shared as brothers from Prayagraj dying by suicide following Akhilesh Yadav’s defeat in UP On Thursday, March 10, Yogi Adityanath scored a major win for the Bharatiya Janata Party in Uttar Pradesh. Amid this, a collage of three photos went viral on social media.Several Facebook users shared the collage, where three different persons could be seen hanging. The claim in Hindi alongside these photos translated to: “Three brothers died by suicide in Prayagraj after watching Akhilesh Yadav getting defeated in the UP polls.”advertisementEMBEDThe India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) found the images had nothing to do with the Uttar Pradesh assembly elections. No such incidents of three brothers dying by suicide took place in Prayagraj, following the poll results.Archived versions of posts with similar claims can be seen here and here.AFWA PROBEWhile investigating the claim, we first conducted a keyword search to find out whether any search incident took place in Prayagraj while the counting process was on. We found no media reports.We then reverse-searched the images and found the source of the first image. Two different news outlets — Sanjeevni Today and Sudama News carried the first photo in reports published in November 2020.According to the reports, the photo is from Ramgarh, where a Bokaro resident Randhir Kumar, 25, died by suicide. We also got in touch with Ajay Kumar, the SSP of Prayagraj. “No such incidents have been reported in Prayagraj,” Kumar told India Today.Although we could not verify the source of the other two photographs used in this claim, we can still confidently conclude that these photos are in no way of three brothers dying by suicide following the results of the UP assembly election.(With inputs from Sanjana Saxena in Lucknow)
label: truth

content: Fact Check: Old video from Bihar circulated as BJP workers attacking man after victory in UP A video of a man being brutally thrashed by others in the presence of policemen has been circulating on social media. The video was shared with the claim that it showed Bharatiya Janata Party members attacking an innocent man after the party’s record win in the recently concluded assembly polls in Uttar Pradesh.The archived versions of similar posts can be seen here, here, and here.advertisementThe India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) found that the claim along with the video was misleading. This video is from Bihar and was shot in 2019.AFWA PROBEWe found the official Twitter handle of UP police's fact check unit responding to a post saying the video in question was from a 2019 incident in Bihar’s Kaimur district, and not related to UP.Taking a cue from this, we ran a keyword search and found screenshots from the same video carried in an India Today report published on October 5, 2019.According to the report, the video showed a ward councillor’s son, accused in a murder case, being attacked in the Shivaji Chowk area of Bhabua in Bihar's Kaimur district. He was accused of shooting a young man who later succumbed to his injuries in a city hospital.The man was later admitted to Kaimur Sadar Hospital for treatment. Kaimur's SP told the media at the time that the deceased was shot over a private dispute with the perpetrator.The Dainik Jagran, Live Hindustan, and News18 reported on the same story in October 2019.According to these reports, the man being thrashed in the video was Shahid Rain. The young man he allegedly shot was Madhav Singh, a resident of Sikhathi village.Reports also added that information about the death of the young man, however, made the public furious and there were attacks at hospitals where Shahid Rain was undergoing treatment. Several local shops were also attacked.It is thus clear that the video in question is old and from Bihar. It has nothing to do with the BJP’s recent victory in UP assembly elections.
label: rumor

content: Fact Check: This heartbreaking video of orphaned children is not from ongoing Ukraine-Russia conflict A heartbreaking video of two children, a girl and a boy, was shared widely on social media with hashtags related to the ongoing Russia-Ukraine crisis.As per the subtitle in the video, both children, when asked about their family, said they lost their fathers in the war. The girl broke into tears when asked if she was getting enough food. The boy was also in tears when asked why he did not have a jacket. He said his family could not afford one anymore.advertisementThe archived versions of similar posts can be seen here, here, and here.The India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) found the video has nothing to do with Russia’s ongoing invasion of Ukraine. The children in the video were from Iraq and Syria.AFWA probeWe ran a reverse search of the keyframes of the video and found the video of the girl uploaded by several YouTube channels in 2017.We also found the same clip in a four-minute-long documentary titled “Malak: The Girl Who Stumbled Out of a War Zone and Stole Our Hearts,” uploaded to the YouTube channel of an aid organisation called Preemptive Love.According to the channel, the girl in this video, Malak, escaped from Fallujah in Iraq with her extended family during the war with ISIS. Her parents were killed in the war. The clip of Malak was shot in 2016, on the day she escaped the war zone to a camp in a desert outside Fallujah.The documentary uploaded by Preemptive Love also showed Malak’s life several months after that day as she settled into a new home with her grandparents.The video was also uploaded on the website of the Global Development Commons, UNICEF’s digital ideas platform to support child-focussed sustainable development goals.Malak’s story is also available on blogs published by Preemptive Love.The video of the boy shared along with the post is also several years old. A screengrab from the video was carried in a Daily Sabah report in February 2020. As per the report, the boy was a Syrian refugee displaced from Idlib.A longer version of the video, where aid workers could be seen providing him with a jacket, was also tweeted by the Daily Sabah.- Where’s your jacket?- My father died and we can’t afford oneTears of young boy show tragedy of Syrian refugees displaced from Idlib due to Assad regime, Russian attackshttps://t.co/qx6bPgeIWG pic.twitter.com/EobZNJNjca — DAILY SABAH (@DailySabah) February 16, 2020The verified Twitter handle of a Turkish news site A Haber also tweeted the longer version of the video. Reportedly, Turkish Interior Minister S¼leyman Soylu asked authorities to locate the boy and provide aid after he saw the video.advertisementIt is thus evident that both the girl and the boy seen in the video have nothing to do with the ongoing Russian invasion of Ukraine.(With inputs from Yash Mittal in New Delhi)READ | Amid heavy shelling, Ukraine’s Mariupol city uses mass graveALSO READ | No, this is not Dynamo Kyiv football squad geared up to face Russian invaders
label: truth

content: Fact Check: Viral video of bulldozer stunt celebrating Yogi Adityanath’s victory in UP is actually from Shanghai As the Bharatiya Janata Party swept the Uttar Pradesh assembly polls, memes depicting Yogi Adityanath’s victory against Akhilesh Yadav through bulldozers crushing bicycles populated social media.While the bicycle is the electoral symbol of the Samajwadi Party, the bulldozer is often used to refer to Yogi Adityanath’s administration being tough on crime — UP authorities have bulldozed illegal properties of members of so-called mafias.advertisementIn fact, calling “bulldozer” a brand for his government, the BJP CM said that the “bulldozer is effective for the expressway and also to run over the mafia.”As the BJP’s victory in UP became apparent on March 10, a short video clip of a bulldozer stunt began making the rounds on Twitter and Facebook with the claim that this was how people were celebrating Yogi Adityanath’s victory.The caption in Hindi on one such viral post reads, “Long live, Bulldozer Baba. There is no limit to the happiness of bulldozers in UP today.”The India Today Anti-Fake News War Room ( AFWA) found that this particular video is from China. In 2016, this bulldozer stunt was shown by a Chinese manufacturing company at an industrial trade fair in Shanghai.The viral posts are archived here and here.AFWA probeWith the help of the InVID tool and reverse image search, we found the original video and details about it.Initially, we found a similar video of the same kind of bulldozer stunt taken from the top on several websites and on YouTube. This video was uploaded to YouTube in June 2017 and the title in Ukrainian language said, “In China, a 17-ton bulldozer danced alongside spectators at a technology show.”In 2017, the same video was shared in news reports on several tech news portals.According to these reports, this bulldozer stunt was performed in a trade fair in China by a Chinese tractor manufacturing company called Lovol. The name Lovol can also be seen written clearly on the bulldozer in the viral video.We also found another YouTube video uploaded to the YouTube channel Foton Lovol with the title, “FotonLovol wheel loader dancing.” This video was uploaded in 2016.Taking all these as clues, with the help of keyword searches, we looked for the viral video and found its longer version on another YouTube channel with a title written in Mongolian language that reads, “Dance loader LOVOL at the Bauma exhibition.” A few seconds into the video, one can see the exact contents of the viral clip.advertisementBauma is an international trade fair for construction machinery, building material machines, mining machines, and construction vehicles. The viral video is from the 2016 fair in Shanghai. The promotional video of the fair was uploaded on their YouTube channel in 2016 and can be seen here.Hence, it is clear that an old video of a bulldozer stunt at a Chinese trade fair has gone viral as that of people celebrating BJP’s victory in UP.
label: truth

content: Fact Check: 2014 Azov Battalion volunteer’s pic shared as Ukrainian soldier saying goodbye to family to join ongoing war against Russia As the Russian invasion of Ukraine continues, so does the stream of misinformation and disinformation surrounding it. Recently, several social media users shared a photo with the claim that it was a “heartbreaking picture from Ukraine” that showed a Ukrainian soldier bidding his family adieu to fight the war.advertisementThe India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) found that the image used in the post was old and not related to the ongoing conflict between Ukraine and Russia.Archived versions of posts with similar claims can be seen here and here.AFWA PROBEWhile investigating the claim, we first reverse-searched the image and found that The Guardian had published it in a news report on November 6, 2017.The caption for the photo stated, “A young woman embraces her boyfriend, a volunteer recruit of the Ukrainian army, in Kyiv in 2014.”Taking this as a cue, we then conducted a keyword search, limiting results to only the year 2014. We found that the Wall Street Journal had published the same photo on June 27, 2014.The caption used with this photo in this article stated, “A woman embraces her boyfriend, a volunteer recruit of the Ukrainian army's Azov battalion, after an oath-swearing ceremony in Kyiv on Monday. About 600 new volunteers of the battalion will join the military operation against pro-Russian militants in the east of the country.”Both The Guardian and the WSJ attributed the photo to Sergei Supinsky of Agence France-Presse (AFP).Hence, we can conclude that the claim in this photo is misleading. While it does feature a Ukrainian soldier, the photo has no connection with the ongoing Russian invasion of Ukraine. The photo is from 2014.
label: rumor

content: Fact Check: Did BSP votes go to BJP in UP? No, years old image of EVM circulated with tampering claims An image of an Electronic Voting Machine (EVM) has been circulating on social media with the claim that the votes cast for the Bahujan Samaj Party in the 2022 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections were registered in favour of the Bharatiya Janata Party.The image was shared with captions that asked people to oppose the use of EVMs in elections.advertisementThe India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) found that the claim along with the image was misleading. This image of the EVM is not recent. It has been circulating on the internet since the 2019 Lok Sabha elections at least.AFWA probeA reverse search of the image in question proved that it was shared online as early as in 2019. We found the same image used by several social media handles in April 2019, at the time of the Lok Sabha elections.We then checked for 2019 news reports surrounding the alleged EVM fraud from Uttar Pradesh.According to reports, during the first phase of polling in the Lok Sabha elections, Dhara Singh, a BSP agent at a polling booth in the Bijnor Lok Sabha constituency made such an allegation. He alleged that the EVM button against the BSP candidate's name and symbol when pressed resulted in votes for the BJP at the Kasoli polling centre.At the time, BSP chief Mayawati asked the Election Commission to take note of this. However, the EC reportedly found the BSP agent’s claim to be incorrect. Dhara Singh was reportedly charged for allegedly spreading "fake news".We found the image of EVM in question carried in the 2019 reports about this incident. The Lallantop, however, noted in its report that the image was old and its source was unknown.From the available details, we can conclude that though the source of the image is unclear, it is at least around three years old and not from the 2022 assembly elections held in UP.ALSO READ | A Modi-Yogi wave that experts spotted too lateALSO READ | All you need to know about the viral video of EVMs being transported in Varanasi
label: truth

content: Fact Check Video: Did Pakistan MPs chant ‘Modi, Modi’ inside Parliament? Prime Minister Narendra Modi attended the Christmas morning service at the Cathedral Church of the Redemption in New Delhi, joining a large congregation for prayers and carols. During the service, the Bishop of Delhi, Church of North India, Paul Swarup, led a special prayer for the Prime Minister, asking for wisdom and strength. Speaking to India Today, Bishop Swarup emphasised that Christmas is primarily a 'message of peace and joy and reconciliation,' which is crucial in a world facing disturbance and wars. He noted that while the Prime Minister did not speak, he participated in the liturgy to pray for the nation. The report also highlights PM Modi's regular engagement with the Christian community, including his attendance at a dinner at Minister George Kurian's residence in 2024.
label: truth

content: Fact Check: All you need to know about the viral video of EVMs being transported in Varanasi Just ahead of the counting of votes for the Uttar Pradesh assembly polls, a video showing a group of Samajwadi Party workers confronting officials transporting Electronic Voting Machines went viral on social media. Alongside the video were allegations of the UP administration trying to manipulate election results by tampering with the EVMs.Soon after the video went viral on March 8, SP chief Akhilesh Yadav accused the Bharatiya Janata Party of “stealing” votes.advertisementThe archived versions of similar posts can be seen here, here, and here.The India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) found the claim misleading. The EVMs caught by the SP workers were reportedly not the ones used for voting. According to the concerned authorities, the EVMs were being transferred for training the counting officers. However, Varanasi’s Commissioner Deepak Agarwal admitted that there were lapses in the protocols for transportation of EVMs.AFWA probeClosely observing the EVM boxes seen in the viral video, we noticed yellow and pink stickers on the boxes with '‘Training/Awareness EVM’’ written on them.As the video went viral and gained the attention of opposition leaders, the District Magistrate of Varanasi clarified to the media that the EVMs were taken for training purposes for officers on counting duty.“Counting workers' 2nd training is scheduled for tomorrow at UP College. 20 EVMs were being taken on a pickup van for hands-on training. These EVMs are always used for training purposes. In UP College, training of 928 counting employees is going on in 16 rooms. The EVMs which were used in the elections are all sealed in the strong room and are in the possession of CRPF and there is CCTV surveillance which is being watched by people of all political parties,” Varanasi Kaushal Raj Sharma said.Counting workers' 2nd training is scheduled for tomorrow at UP College. 20 EVMs were being taken on a pickup van for hands-on training. It was stopped by some people, a confusion arose among them if they were polled EVMs: Kaushal Raj Sharma, Varanasi DM on Akhilesh Yadav's claim pic.twitter.com/hHpWWzA3R6 — ANI UP/Uttarakhand (@ANINewsUP) March 8, 2022The office of Uttar Pradesh’s Chief Electoral Officer also clarified that the EVMs were being brought in Varanasi for training, and insisted that the EVMs used in polling were sealed were under constant surveillance.However, Akhilesh Yadav, during a press meet reportedly claimed that no information was given to his party candidates concerning the transport of the EVMs.advertisement“If the EVMs were being transported for training, why weren’t the candidates informed?” The Indian Express quoted the former UP chief minister saying.Congress party spokesperson Pawan Khera also questioned why training was scheduled just 36 hours before the counting of votes.Varanasi's Commissioner Deepak Agarwal admitted that there were lapses in protocols in the movement of EVMs. However, the officer, while speaking to the media, insisted that the machines in question were only for training purposes.Former IAS officer Sanjeev Gupta had also tweeted that according to the Election Commission protocol, no EVM can be transported without informing the Election Commission.No EVM, whether or not used in polling, can be shifted without informing candidates.EVMs earmarked for training are given separate tag during First Level Check & one should checkEach RO had sufficient time for counting training. Last minute rush was avoidable.@ChiefSecyUP pic.twitter.com/sldeLxg3fG — Sanjeev Gupta (@sanjg2k1) March 9, 2022“Political Parties should necessarily be invited to witness this process from the opening of warehouse and resealing of the warehouse after taking out the EVMs/VVPATs for training and awareness. The entire process to be videographed,” notes chapter 5, section 12 of the Election Commission of India manual on Electronic Voting Machine and VVPAT.advertisementIt is hence clear that while there was a protocol violation in the transport of the EVMs, they were for training purposes.(With inputs from Sanjana Saxena in Lucknow)ALSO READ | Varanasi ADM suspended, 2 UP officials removed from poll duty after SP's EVM tampering chargeALSO READ | Did CMO officials stop taking Yogi Adityanath’s calls? No, viral clip shared with false claims
label: rumor

content: Fact Check: No, this is not Dynamo Kyiv football squad geared up to face Russian invaders Ukrainian footballers Vitalii Sapylo and Dmytro Martynenko were recognised as the football fraternity's first casualties in the ongoing Russia-Ukraine war. Not long after the International Federation of Professional Footballers (FIPRO) broke the news of their demise, another bit of “news” from the conflict zone made splashes across social media.A virally shared post claimed that players from prominent Ukrainian football team Dynamo Kyiv decided to take arms against the invading Russian forces. The claim came along with a group photo of men in military outfits holding guns.advertisementSimilar posts have been archived here and here.The India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) found the claim to be misleading. The men in the picture are not players of the football club.AFWA ProbeWe first checked the official Twitter page of Dynamo Kyiv. The latest updates on the club's verified Twitter page at the time of writing this said it started charitable financing of hospitals that helped those wounded in the conflict. However, there was no information on its direct involvement in military action.A reverse search of the viral image on Bing took us to the verified Facebook account of one Sergey Sternenko. The image shared as that of the footballers was uploaded on the page on February 25, a day after Russia's invasion began."Ready. We are waiting for further orders. May this night be good for Ukraine and eternal for the Russian invaders," the caption read. Sternenko is a Kyiv-based lawyer who is the legal advisor for 'Oscar T', his Facebook bio said.The next result on the search engine, however, was a fact-check report by Reuters. The report said that the social media manager for Dynamo Kyiv, Bogdan Ilyuk, confirmed via email that the picture does not feature any Dynamo Kyiv football players.The report also mentioned Sternenko as a member of a right-wing nationalist group called Gonor.Gonor, in its own words, is a "modern youth movement that seeks independence for Ukraine." Members of the movement made news when they joined the pro-democracy rallies in Hong Kong. You can read more on the group here.Sternenko also uploaded the photo on Instagram with the same caption he used on Facebook.We found the same photo uploaded on the Instagram page of Gonor on February 25. The post was captioned: "Death to the invaders! Glory to the Nation!!!"advertisementWe can thus conclude that the viral photo in question does not feature football players from FC Dynamo Kyiv.READ | Fact Check: No, this is not a Ukrainian tank from the 2003 invasion of IraqALSO READ | Fact Check: This picture of an emotional old man and his cat is not from war-torn Ukraine
label: truth

content: Fact Check: No, this is not a Ukrainian tank from the 2003 invasion of Iraq Amid the ongoing Russian invasion of Ukraine, several people on social media shared a photo of an armoured tank with the Ukrainian flag on its back. The photo was shared with the claim that it was from Ukraine's participation in the 2003 invasion of Iraq. In the photo, the tank could be seen standing in front of a mural of former Iraqi president Saddam Hussein.advertisementOne person shared the photo on Twitter and said, “In 2003, Ukraine invaded Iraq. The tank was sent by the Crusaders to Iraq Destroyed Today. Ukraine itself has been destroyed #RussiaUkraine.”The India Today Anti-Fake News War Room (AFWA) has found the viral image was digitally altered. The Ukrainian flag is missing in the original image. The original photo was taken during Iraq's invasion of Kuwait in 1990.AFWA probeWith the help of reverse image search, we found the image published in an article in 2013 on a news portal.In this image, there was no Ukrainian flag on the back of the armoured tank. The photo caption read, “Pictured: the Iraqi invasion of Kuwait in 1990, which Iraq's new government is still paying the price for.”We compared the two images and it became clear that the viral image was digitally altered.Another photo of the Getty images taken at the same location in Kuwait shows the deployed American soldiers in 1991.The caption on the photo taken by Langevin Jacques said, “U.S. Troops in Kuwait During Persian Gulf War- American soldiers deployed in Kuwait during the Persian Gulf War rest in front of a mural of Saddam Hussein. In August of 1990, Iraqi President Saddam Hussein invaded Kuwait, causing a coalition of countries to deploy troops into the region to expel Iraq from Kuwait.”The Iraq war of 1990-91Following former Iraqi leader Saddam Hussein’s decision to invade the small, oil-rich Kuwait, the United Nations Security Council promptly slapped multiple sanctions on Iraq and demanded the immediate and unconditional withdrawal of Iraqi forces from Kuwait. The UNSC later authorised the use of force to expel Iraqi troops from the country.In February 1991, US-led coalition forces liberated Kuwait from Iraqi forces. Ukraine was not part of this allied coalition force made up of 39 countries in 1990.Iraq war of 2003In March 2003, a combined force of troops from the United States and Great Britain with smaller contingents from several other countries, invaded Iraq vowing to destroy Iraqi weapons of mass destruction (WMD) and end the dictatorial rule of Saddam Hussein. It ended with the fall of the Iraqi army and the capture of Saddam Hussein from Tikrit in December 2003.advertisementAlthough the US and Britain took the lead in attacking Iraq in 2003, several dozen nations contributed to this war against Iraq. Ukraine was also one among these countries.Thus, we conclude that a digitally altered photo from the first Gulf War was shared with the claim that it was from the Ukrainian participation efforts in the 2003 invasion of Iraq.(With inputs from Yash Mittal)READ: Fact Check: This picture of an emotional old man and his cat is not from war-torn UkraineALSO READ: Fact Check: No, this video DOES NOT show protests in Moscow against ongoing Russian invasion of Ukraine
label: truth

content: Fact Check Video: This is not Moscow city protesting against Russian invasion of Ukraine Prime Minister Narendra Modi attended the Christmas morning service at the Cathedral Church of the Redemption in New Delhi, joining a large congregation for prayers and carols. During the service, the Bishop of Delhi, Church of North India, Paul Swarup, led a special prayer for the Prime Minister, asking for wisdom and strength. Speaking to India Today, Bishop Swarup emphasised that Christmas is primarily a 'message of peace and joy and reconciliation,' which is crucial in a world facing disturbance and wars. He noted that while the Prime Minister did not speak, he participated in the liturgy to pray for the nation. The report also highlights PM Modi's regular engagement with the Christian community, including his attendance at a dinner at Minister George Kurian's residence in 2024.
label: truth

content: Fact Check: This picture of an emotional old man and his cat is not from war-torn Ukraine The Russian invasion of Ukraine has led to an influx of posts supposedly depicting Ukrainians overcome with emotion while trying to deal with the war. One such post featured the photo of an old man with his cat in front of a charred house.“Bombs & bullets will never break our bond with our companion animals #StandWithUkraine,” read one such caption on Twitter. Similar posts were shared on Facebook as well.advertisementThe India Today Anti-Fake News War Room (AFWA) found that this photo was taken in 2018 in Turkey. An emotional Ali Mese, 83, from Bolu, Turkey, was photographed after his house was devastated in a fire.AFWA probeWith the help of reverse image search, we found the photo was shared on the internet as early as 2018.We found this image in a TRT World news report on Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoan voting for the Anadolu Agency's Photos of the Year awards. The viral photo, titled “Ali and his cat,” was selected among the best photos of the Turkish news agency. The article was published in December 2018.We found more details about this photo on several Turkish news websites. According to reports, the name of the old man in the photo is Ali Mese.Mese, 83, accidentally set his house on fire while trying to ignite a stove with gasoline in the Mudurnu district of the Bolu province in Turkey in January 2018. The old man was photographed in an emotional state after the firefighters rescued his pet from his charred house.Thus, we conclude that this picture of an old man and his cat is not from Ukraine but Turkey and it is over five years old.
label: truth

content: Fact Check: No, this video DOES NOT show protests in Moscow against ongoing Russian invasion of Ukraine Russian President Vladimir Putin’s invasion of Ukraine has spawned anti-war protests across the world, including in Russia. According to reports, thousands have been detained in Russia so far for protesting against the war.A video from a huge demonstration has been making the rounds on social media, with claims that it is from an anti-war protest in Moscow.The archived versions of similar posts can be seen here, here, and here.advertisementThe India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) found the claim along with the video to be misleading. This video has been on the internet since at least January 2021.AFWA probeWe first noticed that several social media users from Russia pointed out the video was old and not related to the ongoing war. We ran a reverse search of the keyframes of the video on the Russian search engine Yandex and found the same video ( https://www.youtube.com/ watch?app=desktop&v= c1Gg3law1fE ) shared as early as January 23, 2021. As per social media posts, the video was from Moscow and captured a protest against the arrest of the Russian leader and anti-corruption activist Alexei Navalny.Verified Twitter users also shared the video around the same week in January 2021 with the same claim.A view of Navalny’s protest crowd in Moscow, via @bazabazon pic.twitter.com/wopFSWiRFr — Kevin Rothrock (@KevinRothrock) January 23, 2021We then searched for media reports from Russia published in January 2021 surrounding the arrest and subsequent protests. According to a BBC report published on January 23, 2021, thousands of people were detained across Russia after they protested against the arrest of Navalny.On January 17, 2021, Navalny was arrested by the police at Moscow’s Sheremetyevo airport, soon after he landed in the country following medical treatment in Berlin, Germany. According to a report in The Guardian, Navalny’s investigations into corruption in Putin’s inner circle provoked the ire of Russia’s powerbrokers. Following Navalny's arrest, weeks-long protests took place in Russia.We also found several other videos of people protesting the arrest of Navalny in January 2021.Responding to the viral video, BBC journalist Shayan Sardarizadeh also tweeted, saying the video was from the January 2021 protest against Navalny’s arrest.Geolocating the videoAt the beginning of the viral video, we noticed a blue bus similar to the ones found on the roads of Moscow. We cropped the screenshots of a few buildings seen in the video and ran reverse-image searches on Yandex.advertisementThis led us to photos of Tverskaya Street in Moscow. We then searched for the street view of Tverskaya Street on Google and found the same buildings and streets seen in the viral video.The Google Maps location of the street can be seen here. A comparison between screenshots from the viral video and Google Street View of Tverskaya Street can be seen below.We cannot say with absolute certainty that the video in question was from one of the January 2021 protests. However, with the available details, we can conclude that the video, while from Moscow, does not capture anti-war protests against Russia’s ongoing invasion of Ukraine.ALSO READ | Fact Check: No, this old woman is not giving invading Russian soldiers the fingerWATCH | Fact Check Video: 10-year-old video from Canada shared as Russian troops’ movement in Ukraine
label: truth

content: Fact Check: Did CMO officials stop taking Yogi Adityanath’s calls? No, viral clip shared with false claims  As the final phase of the assembly polls in Uttar Pradesh concluded, a video of Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath went viral on social media with some questionable claims.In the video, Adityanath can be heard speaking in Hindi: “This is wrong. It is a common courtesy to answer the phone, or call back later if one is busy”A number of Facebook and Twitter users shared the clip claiming CMO officials have stopped answering Adityanath’s calls, days before UP poll results are to be announced.advertisement“Officials aren’t taking the Chief Minister’s calls,” read one such caption in Hindi. Others predicted a change in regime in Uttar Pradesh.Archived versions of some similar claims can be seen here and here.The India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) found these claims alongside the video to be misleading. The video is old and has nothing to do with the assembly polls.AFWA CheckThe logo of R9 News is clearly visible in the video. Therefore, we searched on the news channel’s YouTube with relevant keywords. We found the original longer news report uploaded to the R9 News YouTube channel on September 26, 2020.In the original news report, the anchor is heard saying Adityanath was unhappy with his officials for not answering public representatives’ calls. At the 38-second mark, Adityanath appeared and said, “This is a serious issue. We learnt from Kanpur and a couple of other places that the CMO did not answer MPs’ and MLAs’ calls.”The UP CM also asked his officials to apologise to the concerned parties in that video. At the 1-minute 14-second mark, the viral clip’s contents can be seen. This made the context of Adityanath’s words clear.The TV news report also revealed that Adityanath made these comments during a review meeting for the Kanpur district and that the CM was upset after receiving complaints from Abhijeet Singh Sanga and Arun Pathak, two local Bharatiya Janata Party MLAs.The date of the meeting was revealed in the R9 News clip. Consequently, we ran a keyword search with the information available and it led us to an ANI tweet from September 25, 2020. The tweet read, “Lucknow: UP CM Yogi Adityanath held a review meeting for developmental projects of Kanpur district via video conferencing, yesterday.”Lucknow: UP CM Yogi Adityanath held a review meeting for developmental projects of Kanpur district via video conferencing, yesterday. pic.twitter.com/CCDUkUsOCG — ANI UP/Uttarakhand (@ANINewsUP) September 24, 2020When we compared the photos in the tweet to the news clip, it became clear that both the pictures are from the same meeting which took place on September 24, 2020.Thus, we conclude that the viral video of Yogi Adityanath was clipped from a news report and shared with false claims.
label: rumor
