content: Fact Check: 2016 video of gun-toting men at SP rally passed off as recent incident in Meerut With two phases down and the third just days away in the Uttar Pradesh assembly polls, a video featuring a group of young men brandishing guns and firing them in the open has gone viral with the claim that this was shot recently at the reception of a Samajwadi Party leader.Several Facebook and Twitter users shared the video with captions like: “Hundreds of illegal firearms were brandished during an SP procession. Guns were fired at the reception of Nawazish, the son of former SP cabinet minister and assembly polls candidate Shahid Manzoor. The video of them dancing with weapons at the procession has gone viral. The viral video is from the Kithore Assembly constituency. The gun-toting Samajwadi Party.”advertisementLawyer and Bharatiya Janata Party spokesperson Prashant Patel Umrao shared the viral video with the same claim.India Today Anti-Fake News War Room ( AFWA) found the claim misleading. The viral video is more than five years old and is not related to the ongoing elections in Uttar Pradesh.AFWA probeSoon after the video went viral, the Uttar Pradesh police refuted the claim by tweeting that it was from 2016.But the police could not provide any visual evidence in support of their claim. When AFWA contacted Prabhakar Chaudhary, the SSP of Meerut, his office only reiterated that the viral video was from 2016, and that they were still investigating the matter.AFWA tried every possible combination of keywords and searched the internet, narrowing the timeline down to 2016, but failed to find any videos related to the incident.India Today’s Meerut correspondent Usman Chaudhary confirmed that the man in a white kurta seen at the last part of the viral video was indeed local Samajwadi Party leader Nawazish Alam Khan, the son of former SP cabinet minister and assembly polls candidate Shahid Manzoor.Since the claim is around Nawazish Alam Khan, AFWA contacted the SP leader from Meerut. Over the phone, Khan confirmed that it was indeed him in the viral video.“It was in 2016, I was at an election campaign rally in the Radhna Inayatpur village of Meerut for the Zilla Panchayat elections. There were some local goons led by Umar Ali who were firing in open air, which I disliked. The same day, I expelled Umar Ali from the party and he joined the BJP as their agent.” claimed Khan.With the location of Radhna Inayatpur as a possible clue, we once again searched for the video and found the exact video uploaded on YouTube by a user on October 27, 2017. The title of the YouTube video reads, “Radhana Inayatpur ma aaved hatiyro ka shaath Umar Ali our ous ka gang” or “Umar Ali and his gang seen with illegal weapons in Radhna Inayatpur.”advertisementThe YouTube video is a little longer than one going viral. At the start, we can see some young people dancing with a kid on their shoulders and arms in their hands. One can also see a water tank distinctly in the background.Geo locating the spotAFWA tried to look for local contacts from Radhna Inayatpur. We also chanced upon the number of a local mosque in Radhna Inayatpur. We contacted Mohd. Nazish, the administrator of the Haji Tosif Wali Masjid.Nazish watched the viral video and confirmed that it was indeed from Radhna Inayatpur. “This incident took place in 2016. Police action was taken against the people seen with firearms in the video. The water tank is located at the entry point of our Radhna Inayatpur village.”AFWA requested Mohd. Nazish to send a recent video or a recent picture from the location seen in the viral video showing the water tank. Subsequently, he sent us a recent video from the exact spot seen in the viral video with the landmark water tank in the background.The exact location is Amarpur Mazra Khandawli and the road seen in the viral video leads to Mawana from Kithore, as identified on Google Maps.Video sent by a local resident of Radhna Inayatpur village. Thus, based on all the evidence, it is clear that the viral video is over five years old and not linked to ongoing polls in UP. label: truth

content: Fact Check: Old image of truckers’ convoy passed off as recent protest against Covid-19 mandates in Canada Canadian Prime Minister Justin Trudeau on Monday, February 14, invoked the Emergencies Act to bring an end to truckers-led protests against mandatory Covid-19 vaccination. Amid this, a photo of a long nose-to-tail queue of trucks lined up on a highway has gone viral with the claim that this was the "Freedom Convoy" of truckers who travelled to Canada’s capital to protest the vaccine mandates.advertisementSeveral Facebook users shared the photo with a long caption that blamed the mainstream media for not giving enough coverage to this protest.The caption read, “Huge shoutout to mainstream media for downplaying the convoy. Huge shoutout to the towns and cities that shut their traffic cameras off when the convoy went through. Huge shoutout to Justin Trudeau for hiding in his bedroom just before the convoy gets to Ottawa. Huge shoutout to Facebook for deleting the original convoy page. Huge shoutout to GoFundMe for trying to tie up the money that's for the truckers and their support. You've all shown how important this convoy really is.”India Today Anti-Fake news War Room (AFWA) found that the viral photo had nothing to do with the recent truckers’ protests. The photo, in fact, shows a rally held by truckers in 2019 in support of the oil and gas industry in Canada.We reverse-searched the image and found it in a CTV News report from February 14, 2019, titled, “Truck convoy heads to Ottawa to protest lack of pipeline progress”.The caption of the photo read, “A convoy of at least 100 trucks is driving from Alberta to Parliament Hill to draw attention to what it says is Ottawa’s lack of support for the energy sector.” As per the report, in 2019, Canadian truckers drove to Ottawa, and the convoy was called "United We Roll". The truckers protested the Canadian government's energy policies.Courtesy - CTV NewsCanada has been witnessing an uproar against vaccine mandates for a few weeks now. In January 2022, a convoy of thousands of truckers and other protesters gathered on Parliament Hill to demonstrate against vaccine mandates.The viral image, however, is three years old and it has no connection to the recent truckers’ strike in Canada.
label: rumor

content: Fact Check: No, Akhilesh Yadav did not misbehave with doctor because he was Brahmin A video of Samajwadi Party supremo Akhilesh Yadav went viral with the claim that the former chief minister of Uttar Pradesh misbehaved with a senior doctor at a hospital in Kannauj because he was Brahmin.Several Facebook users shared a 28-second-long video where Yadav can be heard scolding a man and asking him to leave the place. Facebook users have claimed that Yadav misbehaved with Dr. DS Mishra. a senior physician at a Kannauj hospital, because he was Brahmin.advertisementIn Hindi, the viral posts claimed, “Akhilesh Yadav’s attitude towards senior doctor DS Mishra in Kannauj betrays his mentality. After asking the name. The way Akhilesh treated him after realising he was Brahmin; Does the SP supremo think being a Brahmin is sinful?”India Today Anti-Fake News War Room (AFWA) found this claim misleading. In 2020, while meeting hospitalised victims of a bus accident in Kannauj, Yadav drove a medical officer out of the ward. The officer told reporters Yadav lost his temper because one patient complained about not receiving a compensatory cheque. The doctor, however, told Yadav the patient had received it.AFWA probeWith the help of keywords search we have found the viral video on YouTube uploaded in January 2020 by The Times of India. The title reads, “SP President Akhilesh Yadav drives Kannauj doctor away from ward, says ‘tum bhaag jaao’”As per the news report, Yadav visited a hospital to meet those injured in the bus accident. A bus with over 40 passengers collided with a truck in Uttar Pradesh's Kannauj and caught on fire on January 10. 2020.Taking this as a clue, with the help of a keywords-search, we have found a longer version of the video, and taken from a different camera angle. It was shared by the news agency ANI on January 14, 2020.The caption of the ANI tweet reads, “Former CM Akhilesh Yadav who went to meet injured of Kannauj accident, at a hospital in Chhibramau asks Emergency Medical Officer to leave the room as he speaks about compensation amount been given to the injured,says, ‘Tum sarkar ka paksh nahi le sakte...bahar bhaag jao’.”In the video, one can hear a man standing beside the injured complaining that the victim had not received a compensatory “cheque”. Somebody from the background refuted this and said, “He has received it.”Yadav then told the second man, “You shouldn’t talk because you are a government official. You will take the side of the government. You may be an RSS or a BJP man , but you are a very junior official. So, you do not have to interpret what he is saying. You get lost from here. Just leave the place.”advertisement#WATCH Former CM Akhilesh Yadav who went to meet injured of Kannauj accident, at a hospital in Chhibramau asks Emergency Medical Officer to leave the room as he speaks about compensation amount been given to the injured,says, "Tum sarkar ka paksh nahi le sakte...bahar bhaag jao". pic.twitter.com/U3DrdHI1se — ANI UP/Uttarakhand (@ANINewsUP) January 14, 2020We found that multiple news outlets who reported this in January 2020, sharing with same video.According to these news reports, while meeting the injured, Yadav was informed by a patient party that they did not receive the compensatory cheque from the government. But the emergency medical officer of the hospital Dr. DS Mishra, who was present there, tried to refute this claim. Yadav, annoyed with this, scolded the officer, and asked him to leave the place immediately.Later, ANI reported quoting Mishra that the medical officer was present there because he was treating patients. “One of the patients said he didn't get the compensation cheque. I tried to clarify that the cheque was given. At this, former CM Akhilesh ji got angry and asked me to leave the room,” said Dr Mishra.Thus, it can be concluded that the viral claim saying Akhilesh Yadabv scolded a doctor in Kannauj hospital because he was Brahmin is false.
label: truth

content: Fact Check Video: Video of BJP-TRS clash in Telangana shared as violence against BJP workers in UP Prime Minister Narendra Modi attended the Christmas morning service at the Cathedral Church of the Redemption in New Delhi, joining a large congregation for prayers and carols. During the service, the Bishop of Delhi, Church of North India, Paul Swarup, led a special prayer for the Prime Minister, asking for wisdom and strength. Speaking to India Today, Bishop Swarup emphasised that Christmas is primarily a 'message of peace and joy and reconciliation,' which is crucial in a world facing disturbance and wars. He noted that while the Prime Minister did not speak, he participated in the liturgy to pray for the nation. The report also highlights PM Modi's regular engagement with the Christian community, including his attendance at a dinner at Minister George Kurian's residence in 2024.
label: truth

content: Fact Check: Photo of 2016 Quetta police academy suicide-bombing shared as victims of BLA strike in Panjgur A twin strike by Balochistan Liberation Army (BLA) rebels on Pakistani army posts at Panjgur and Noshki claimed the lives of nine soldiers earlier this month. Following the attack, Islamabad denied claims by the insurgents that at least a hundred soldiers were killed in the attacks.A photo shared by pro-BLA handles on social media claims to be the coffins of Pakistan personnel killed in the Panjgur operation. "#PakistanArmy Daal koor army dead bodies from Panjgur not countable more then 100 body's some of body's SSG commands body's," one such tweet read.advertisementIndia Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) found the claim to be misleading. The image shared was shot in 2016, when suicide bombers infiltrated the Quetta police training academy and killed 59 people.Similar posts are archived here and here.AFWA probeWhen we reverse-searched the image, we found it used in an article by prominent Pakistan news outlet Dawn. The report was a photo story from October 25, 2016, on the devastation caused by the terrorist attack.The photo now in circulation, claimed to be from Panjgur, was included in the photo story with the caption, "Coffins of cadets killed during the attack on the police training college being lined up for funeral prayers at the General Musa Stadium — APP."The same photo was also used by the news website called Urdupoint.com with similar information. "QUETTA: Bodies of martyr cadets of Police Training Centre carnage being brought at Musa Stadium Quetta Cantt for funeral prayers," the caption accompanying the picture read.The Islamic State had reportedly carried out the deadly attack with the support of Afghanistan based-Lashkar-e-Jhangvi. On the night of October 24, 2016, three heavily armed militants entered the academy while around 700 cadets were asleep.Two attackers detonated their suicide vests, causing most of the casualties, while the third was killed before he could carry out the suicide-bombing. Over 150 people were injured in the incident. You can read more about the attack here and here.Thus, it is clear that the photo of coffins wrapped in Pakistani flags was not of the mortal remains of soldiers killed in the attack by the Balochistan Liberation Army (BLA) earlier this month. The image was taken after the 2016 suicide-bombings at Quetta's police training academy.
label: rumor

content: Fact Check: Did SAD's Sukhbir Singh Badal seek Gurmeet Ram Rahim’s support in assembly polls? With assembly polls in Punjab scheduled for February 20, social media is abuzz with news, views, and of course, hoaxes surrounding the upcoming event. Of the viral misleading posts, one is a screenshot of a news report.Several people on social media shared a screengrab of a Punjabi news report that translates to, “Hailing Baba Ram Rahim as the father of Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD), party President Sukhbir Singh Badal has asked him to support SAD.”advertisementThe report states that Badal has hailed Dera Sacha Sauda’s chief Gurmeet Ram Rahim during a press conference in Chandigarh on February 11.India Today Anti-Fake News War room (AFWA) found that the viral screenshot was morphed. Badal had never made this statement.Archived versions of posts with similar claims can be seen here and here.AFWA PROBESukhbir Singh Badal’s StatementWhile investigating the claim we first carried out a keyword search to find out if Badal had indeed made any statement on the 21-day furlough granted to Ram Rahim.Media reports state that while speaking to media in Rupnagar on February 8, Badal termed the furlough granted to Dera Sacha Sauda chief as a Bharatiya Janata Party election stunt.It therefore seems unlikely that Badal would then resort to making such a statement.Where was Sukhbir Singh Badal on February 11?The viral news report clearly states that Badal had praised Ram Rahim and sought his support during a press conference in Chandigarh on February 11. We tried to find out whether any such press conference was held on February 11 in Chandigarh. We conducted another keyword search.We found a Times of India report that said Badal was on an election campaign on February 11 in Ferozepur. He was in Ferozepur to campaign in favour of party candidate Vardev Singh Noni Mann in Guruharsahai, Joginder Singh Jindu in Ferozepur Rural, and Rohit Kumar Montu Vohra in Ferozepur urban.To further confirm the claim, we got in touch with Joginder Singh Jindu, the SAD candidate from Ferozepur Rural.“Sukhbir Singh Badal was in Ferozepur district on February 11. He had attended at least seven programmes and was in the district till around 7:30pm on that day,” Jindu confirmed to India Today.The possibility of a press conference in Chandigarh on February 11 is thus suspect because Badal was busy campaigning in Ferozepur, around 223 kilometres away from Chandigarh on that day.This screenshot was morphedThe viral screenshot had no mention of the newspaper that carried this article. We examined the font and style of the report and tried to find out the source for the news report. E found that the style and font matched with the Daily Ajit — a leading Punjabi newspaper.Although the format of the dateline in the Daily Ajit is almost similar to the viral news report, there’s one major difference. In the dateline, the Daily Ajit doesn't mention the year of publication along the date of publication. But in the viral screenshot, the year is also mentioned. We did not find this report on the Daily Ajit’s epaper dated February 11.We got in touch with Satnam Singh Manak, the executive editor of the Daily Ajit. “Although the font and style of the screenshot used in the Facebook post is similar to our publication, we have not carried any such article. Second, in the screenshot, the name of the reporter is given. But we have no such reporter in Chandigarh,” Manak told India Today.Thus, we can conclude that this claim is false. Sukhbir Singh Badal never made such a statement. The screenshot of the newspaper report appears morphed.(With inputs from Yash Mittal in New Delhi)
label: truth

content: Fact Check Video: Arvind Kejriwal did not say he is a BJP-RSS man; viral video is edited In this exclusive interview, former US Ambassador to Ukraine William Taylor analyses the high-stakes diplomatic meetings involving Donald Trump’s envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff in Moscow and Berlin. Speaking to the host, Ambassador Taylor discusses reports that Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy is willing to 'withdraw their request for membership of NATO for the time being' in exchange for alternative security guarantees. He explains the concept of a European-led 'coalition of the willing' to secure Ukraine, distinct from NATO. Taylor also assesses the crumbling of the post-Cold War security architecture and the necessity for Europe to fend for itself against Russian aggression.
label: truth

content: Fact Check: No, Arvind Kejriwal did not say he is a BJP-RSS man; viral video doctored Amid the ongoing assembly polls in five states, where Aam Aadmi Party is also a contender, a video clip has gone viral featuring Delhi Chief Minister and party supremo Arvind Kejriwal.This seven-second clip was shared by many with the claim that in it, Kejriwal admitted to his ties with the Bharatiya Janata Party and the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh. In that video, Kejriwal can be heard saying in Hindi, “We come from a Jan Sangh family. We have been life-long BJP supporters. My father, who belonged to Jan Sangh, was jailed during the emergency.”advertisement“Kejriwal admits he is a BJP-RSS man,” a Twitter user claimed sharing the video. The official handle of Dadra and Nagar Haveli Congress Sevadal has also shared this video alongside a caption that reads, “We have already been telling this. It's now wide and open. Kejriwal is BJP/RSS Pawn. Paidaieshi BJP wale hain ye.”We have aalready been telling this.It's now wide and open.Kejriwal is BJP/RSS Pawn.Paidaieshi BJP wale hain ye.#AAP_BJP_Exposed pic.twitter.com/o0CJ5DhTyy — Dadra and Nagar Haveli Congress Sevadal (@SevadalDNH) February 13, 2022Archived versions of similar claims can be seen here, here, and here.India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) found this claim to be misleading. The viral video has been doctored. Kejriwal in the original video was referring to another person; not himself.AFWA ProbeThe logo of NDTV 24X7 was clearly visible in this video. So, we searched for a source with relevant keywords.Search results led us to a video uploaded by the NDTV on YouTube on February 4, 2020. At the 4.11-minute-mark, Kejriwal can be heard criticising the top BJP leadership for seeking votes against the issue of anti-CAA protest in Shaheen Bagh. At that time, the 2020 Delhi Assembly Elections were around the corner.At the one-minute-39-seconds mark, Kejriwal said in Hindi, “I was watching a channel where a BJP-man was speaking. He said ‘We come from a Jan Sangh family. We have been life-long BJP supporters. My father, who belonged to Jan Sangh, was jailed during the emergency. But this time I’ll vote for Kejriwal.’”In the viral clip, the first and the last part of Kejriwal’s words have been edited out. We also found an NDTV news report about this interview.Thus, it is clear that the viral video of Arvind Kejriwal where he said he was a BJP-RSS man was edited to give it a false context.(With Inputs from Sanjana Saxena in Lucknow)
label: truth

content: Fact Check: Video of BJP-TRS clash in Telangana shared as violence against BJP workers in Uttar Pradesh A video of a scuffle has gone viral on social media. Many have shared the clip, in which a handful of Bharatiya Janata Party workers can be seen attacked in broad daylight, claiming this took place in Uttar Pradesh amid the assembly polls. One such tweet can be seen here.Similar claims have been archived here.India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) found the claim misleading. The video is from Telangana's Jangaon district. The video shows BJP workers clashing with members of the ruling Telangana Rashtra Samithi. The incident has no connection to the ongoing polls in UP.AFWA ProbeWhen we searched, we found no recent reports of major political clashes in UP. Upon a closer look at the video, we noticed the writing on one of the traffic islands. It said "Jangaon Traffic Police.”Jangaon is a district in Telangana — located 85 kilometres away from Hyderabad. The people chasing the BJP workers donned pink shawls. Pink is the dominant colour of the TRS — the state’s ruling party. We also confirmed that in the video, the language on the storefront signs (aside from English) was Telugu.We spotted a huge billboard towards the end of the video with the photo and name of K Chandrasekhar Rao a.k.a. KCR — the chief minister of Telangana, and the TRS supremo.This confirmed that the video is not from Uttar Pradesh as claimed by many; rather it was shot in Telangana.We ran a Google keyword search to learn more about the clash. According to media reports, the incident took place on February 9, 2022, when workers of the two parties faced off.On February 8, Prime Minister Narendra Modi had told the Rajya Sabha that the bifurcation of Andhra Pradesh in 2014 was not a smooth affair. He said there was no consultation over the process and consequently, both Telangana and Andhra Pradesh suffered.The Prime Minister's remarks weren't well-received by the TRS who decided to organise protests against him. On February 9, Jangaon MLA Muthireddy Yadagiri Reddy called upon TRS members to stage a protest against the PM. Party workers organised a motorcycle rally.The TRS' decision to burn an effigy of Modi in the town was contended by flag-bearing BJP supporters who arrived at the spot, reports state. This led to a physical confrontation between the two groups during which the video in circulation was shot. A detailed report of the incident can be read here.We also found the viral video on the YouTube channel of TV9 Telugu uploaded on February 9.Another popular Telugu channel, NTV Telugu had more visuals of the incident.advertisementThus, it is clear that the video in circulation captures a tussle between BJP and TRS workers in the Jangaon district of Telangana. It has nothing to do with either Uttar Pradesh or the ongoing assembly polls there.(With inputs from Sanjana Saxena in Lucknow)
label: truth

content: Fact Check: Decade-old video of Yogi Adityanath distributing money shared with claims of bribery during assembly polls With six more phases of the Uttar Pradesh assembly polls yet to take place, social media is full of supporters of various parties attempting to influence the electorate. Amid this, a video of UP Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath distributing money has been shared by several people.The viral video sees the CM sitting in a chair, surrounded by people. A few people were seen touching his feet after receiving money. Those sharing the video accused the CM of bribing voters during the ongoing assembly elections.advertisement“This is how he’s contesting. For the first time in this country’s history, we are witnessing a Chief Minister distributing money to win elections,” claimed a Twitter user. The video has also gone viral on Facebook with the same claim.Archived version of the same claim can be found here and here.India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) found this claim misleading. The viral video is about a decade old and has nothing to do with the ongoing assembly elections.AFWA ProbeWith the help of InVid, we sliced the video into key frames. Through reverse search of the images, we found several fact-check reports based on this video.Results led us to a fact-check report on the same video published by The Quint on March 23, 2019. The report noted that this video initially went viral just before the 2019 Lok Sabha Elections.India Today also fact-checked the same claim during the Lok Sabha elections. That report mentioned that this viral video was actually from 2012 and had nothing to do with the then-ongoing polls.The original video was uploaded by a person called Vinay Kumar Gautam in 2012. He spoke to AFWA and confirmed that it was shot in April 2012. At that time, Yogi Adityanath was a Lok Sabha MP from Gorakhpur. According to Gautam, several people in and around Gorakhpur faced a huge financial crisis at the time after they lost their crops to a fire. The then-MP reached out to these villagers and helped them financially using the MP fund. However, later Goutam deleted this video from YouTube.Thus, we conclude that the viral video of Yogi Adityanath distributing money is about a decade old and has nothing to do with the ongoing election.(With inputs from Riddhish Dutta)
label: truth

content: Fact Check: Old ‘ragging’ video from Sri Lanka shared as Muslim students harassed by Hindu extremists amid hijab row Amid the Karnataka hijab row, a video has gone viral, in which, a group of young men can be seen throwing buckets of water on burqa-clad women.Several social media users shared this video with the claim that the video showed extremist Hindu men throwing dirty water at Muslim women.Muslim girls have been tortured on the streets of India for the last 4 days. Due to wearing hijab in religious dress. The video shows extremist Hindu people throwing dirty water on Muslim girls on the side of the road. https://t.co/p1HSr6NMlL" >pic.twitter.com/p1HSr6NMlL a> — Shahinur Alam Sumon (@modern_sas) https://twitter.com/ modern_sas/status/ 1491684605216407554?ref_src= twsrc%5Etfw">February 10, 2022advertisementWhile some have claimed that these young men are members of the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh, others claimed them to be members of the Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad, a student organisation affiliated to the RSS.India Today Anti-Fake News War Room (AFWA) found the claims misleading. The video has nothing to do with the ongoing hijab row. In fact, this video is not from India. It is an old video from Sri Lanka.AFWA PROBEUsing InVid and reverse image search, we traced the source of the video. A few social media users had shared this video in February 2019. They claimed the video showed Eastern University students in Sri Lanka hazing juniors.Subsequently, we did a keyword search and found the same video published with the same claim on a Facebook page called Lanka Sun-News on February 24, 2019.https://www.facebook.com/ plugins/video.php?height=313& href=https%3A%2F%2Fwww. facebook.com%2FLankaSunNew% 2Fvideos%2F486275322112251%2F& show_text=false&width=560&t=0" width="560" height="313" style="border:none;overflow: hidden" scrolling="no" frameborder="0" allowfullscreen="true" allow="autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; picture-in-picture; web-share" allowFullScreen="true">iframe>The video was also published by Puthithu — a news website run by Sri Lankan Tamils living abroad — on February 24, 2019. The report claimed that its reporter had confirmed with Eastern University students that the video was indeed filmed on their campus.So, we can safely conclude that the video has no connection with the ongoing hijab row in Karnataka. The video was shot in 2019 in Sri Lanka and showed students of Eastern University hazing other students.(With inputs from Sajana Saxena in Lucknow)
label: rumor

content: Fact Check: Old video of Bangladesh cleric hitting out at Yati Narsinghanand goes viral amid Karnataka Hijab row Amid the Karnataka hijab row, a video of a man has gone viral with the claim that he threatened all Hindus with dire consequences if they did not convert to Islam.Several Twitter users shared the video that declared in Hindi text, “These people have decided your fate. They are just waiting for Modi to be out of the picture. Let’s ensure that all our Hindu brothers are aware of this. Hindus, see this with clear eyes and hear this with your ears clear. Use WhatsApp to make sure every Hindu brother in your contacts list sees this.”advertisementSome Twitter users even shared the video with the trending hashtag #KarnatakaHijabRow.In the 29-second-long clip, a man can be heard speaking in Hindi. He says, “There is still time. Repent. Ask for forgiveness from God's messenger. Or your body won't even be burnt. Vultures, crows, and jackals will feed on your body.” Then, after a jump cut, the man says, “I am inviting you, read the Kalma and become a Muslim. If you want deliverance, read the Kalma and become a Muslim.”India Today Anti-Fake News War Room (AFWA) found that the viral video was edited. The person in the video is Saeed Irshad Ahmed Al Bukhari of Dinajpur, Bangladesh. He was responding to Yati Narsinghanand's comments on Islam.AFWA probeWith the help of InVid and reverse image search, we found that a longer version of the same video was tweeted in May 2021. In the caption, journalist Swati Goel Sharma wrote, “Friendly message from Bangladesh: Corona pandemic and the many deaths and cremations in India is because of 'blasphemy' by Narsinghanand. Hindus, do tauba, otherwise your dead bodies won't be cremated but eaten by cheel-kawwe. Ae pandit Narsinghanand, accept our Islam.”Using this as a clue, with the help of keyword search, we found the original video on Facebook, belonging to one Dr Syed Irshad Ahmad Al Bukhari. The original video was over seven minutes long and it was posted on April 30, 2021.According to the Bengali caption of the Facebook post, the man delivering the speech, Bukhari. And he had arranged a human chain in the Dinajpur district of Bangladesh to protest the controversial comments made by Hindu religious leader Yati Narsinghanand against Islam. According to his Facebook profile, Bukhari is a lecturer at the Islamic Research Centre in Dinajpur, Bangladesh.Missing contextListening carefully to the entire speech delivered by Syed Irshad Ahmed Al Bukhari, we confirmed that the viral clip was an edited one and the relevant portions have been chopped out in the viral clip to give a different context to it.Bukhari began his speech with, “Today we’ve gathered here in Dinajpur, Bangladesh, after the Jumma’s Namaz just to say one thing. That India’s shameless and wicked Pandit Narsinghanand Saraswati, who has insulted and disrespected our Rasool Allah, we just want to say that we two crore Muslims of the world are ready to sacrifice our lives on our Rasool Allah’s feet.”advertisementSo, the context of his speech can be established as a protest against Narsinghanand. But only a small part of his speech was forked out and used in the viral clip. The viral clip also has a jump cut in between two frames, which suggests the clip was edited deliberately to give it a different colour.In the last half of the original video, the man can be heard saying, “In a list of 100 religious teachers’ names, Rasool Allah was at the first position. It was a Christian who kept Rasool Allah at the top of the list; that a Christian recognizes who Rasool Akhal Akhal is, but Narsinghanand Saraswati, you don’t have enough knowledge to understand that.”Then he kept on saying, addressing Narsinghanand: “I am inviting you to read the Kalma and become a Muslim. If you want deliverance, read the Kalma and become a Muslim.”Thus, we confirm that the viral clip was edited deliberately to give it a different context. We also confirmed that the speech was not delivered in India but in Bangladesh. And finally, it has nothing to do with the Karnataka Hijab row.(With input from Yash Mittal)
label: truth

content: Fact Check: No, Mayawati hasn't pledged support to BJP in UP assembly polls, viral video old A video clip featuring Bahujan Samaj Party supremo Maywati has gone viral with the claim that she recently announced her party would support the Bharatiya Janata Party — or any other party — in pursuit of defeating the Samajwadi Party in the soon-to-begin assembly polls in Uttar Pradesh.Several people shared the viral clip featuring the BBC’s logo on Facebook and Twitter, claiming this to be a recent announcement. In the viral clip, Mayawati read out a statement in Hindi: “The BSP will do everything to defeat the SP's second candidate. And to do this, if it is required for our party MLAs to sacrifice their votes to the BJP — or any other party — we will even do that.”advertisementIndia Today Anti-Fake News War Room ( AFWA) found that this viral clip is from October 2020. At the time, Mayawati had said her party would vote for the BJP or any other party's candidate in the then-upcoming Uttar Pradesh MLC elections to defeat the SP's “second candidate.” In the ongoing election campaign in Uttar Pradesh, Mayawati has criticised both the BJP and the SP.The viral posts are archived here and here.AFWA probeSince the viral clip contained the BBC logo, with the help of keywords searches, we found the original video embedded in an article on the BBC website, published on November 2, 2020. This clip is over three minutes long.The same viral clip was also tweeted by news agency ANI on October 29, 2020. The caption of the tweet read, “#WATCH BSP Chief Mayawati says that her party will vote for BJP or any party's candidate in future UP MLC elections, to defeat Samajwadi Party's second candidate. ‘Any party candidate, who'll be dominant over SP's 2nd candidate, will get all BSP MLAs' vote for sure,’ she said.”#WATCH BSP Chief Mayawati says that her party will vote for BJP or any party's candidate in future UP MLC elections, to defeat Samajwadi Party's second candidate."Any party candidate, who'll be dominant over SP's 2nd candidate, will get all BSP MLAs' vote for sure," she said. pic.twitter.com/ki4W6ZAwgE — ANI (@ANI) October 29, 2020This was reported by other news outlets and YouTube channels as well, around the same time.As per these news reports, a few months before the polls to 12 Uttar Pradesh Legislative Council seats, to be held on January 28, 2021, Mayawati announced in October 2020 that her party would vote for any other political outfit, including the BJP, in order to ensure the defeat of the SP in the then-upcoming elections to the Upper House of the Uttar Pradesh Assembly, and the Rajya Sabha.But Mayawati may not have the same views now. The BSP leader has attacked both the BJP and the SP in her recent election campaigns. As per news reports, on February 5, during a BSP election rally in Saharanpur, she has slammed both parties for their “anti-Dalit politics” and urged voters to support the BSP in the upcoming assembly elections and reject the BJP, the SP, and even the Congress.advertisementHence, we conclude that this clip of Mayawati supporting the BJP is misleading, in the context of the upcoming assembly polls in Uttar Pradesh.READ | Youth from Bihar didn't hack into Google, nor was he offered Rs 3.66 cr job
label: truth

content: Fact Check: Did Bhagwant Mann call Kejriwal a robber? No, viral video is doctored Weeks before the Punjab assembly elections and amid the on-going high-octane political campaigning, a video of Aam Aadmi Party’s (AAP) chief ministerial candidate Bhagwant Singh Mann has gone viral where he can be heard saying that Kejriwal robbed everything from a family whose daughter was about to get married.Multiple Facebook and Twitter users have shared this viral clip where Mann can be seen delivering the tale in Punjabi language.advertisementThe audio roughly translates to: “A well-to-do family organised their daughter’s wedding. For the dowry, they bought expensive sofas, a television, expensive suits, utensils, trunks, and jewellery. The baraat was scheduled to arrive the next day. A night before the baraat’s arrival, Kejriwal got to know that they have so much stuff at their home. Kejriwal got a truck, parked it in their home and locked the girl’s whole family in a room. Then he packed everything — from the sofas to the suits to the jewellery and the sweets — in his truck. Right before leaving, Kejriwal gave the girl Rs 500 as shagun (blessing) for the wedding. The next day, the family didn’t file an FIR with the police saying that they might have stolen everything, but they were good people since they gave their daughter shagun.”The viral clip has been posted on Facebook with a caption, "Bhagwant Mann speaks the truth when he's drunk."India Today Anti-Fake News War room ( AFWA) found that the viral clip is doctored. In the original video Bhagwant Mann said “daaku” or dacoits or robbers. Not Kejriwal.AFWA probeWith the help of InVID and reverse image search, we found the original video. The original video of Bhagwant Mann’s speech was uploaded by his verified YouTube channel on December 23, 2021. The same video was uploaded by the YouTube channel of Aam Aadmi Party PunjabFrom the title, we inferred that he was delivering the speech during a rally in the Dinanagar constituency in Punjab.Just past the 5-minute-55-second mark in the YouTube video uploaded by Bhagwant Mann, one can hear the exact portion of the viral speech.Bahgwant Mann was attacking the Punjab CM Charanjit Singh Channi satirically by comparing him to a “daaku” or a robber, who steals everything but tries to atone himself by doing a small good.Mann said “Daakus gave the girl Rs 500 as shagun (blessing) for the wedding. The next day, the family didn’t file an FIR with the police saying they might have stolen everything but they were good people as they gave their daughter shagun. This is exactly what Channi was doing. They were looting Punjab for the last 4.5 years and now they are giving shagun to doli cars”.advertisementThis was in reference to Channi giving "shagun" to a random married couple on the road. It was reported by news outlets that in September last year, the Punjab CM, during his tour to Bhatinda, halted his convoy when he spotted a newly married couple at village Mandi Kalan. Channi reportedly hugged the man and gave “shagun” to his wife after alighting from his vehicle.Hence, it is clear that a doctored video of AAP candidate Bhagwant Mann has gone viral. Mann in the original video did not mention Kejriwal. Rather he said “daaku” or robber to narrate a satirical story.( with input from Yash Mittal)
label: rumor

content: Fact Check: Old photos of Mumbai college Independence Day celebration crop up in Karnataka hijab row Karnataka is at the centre of a political storm as the row over hijabs in educational institutions refuses to die down. A month after six women were barred from entering classes for wearing the hijab at a Women’s Government PU College in Udupi, protests and counter-protests have now spread across several college campuses. More than 100 male students went for classes wearing saffron shawls on February 2. On February 5, 200 boys in Bhandarkar's College, Kundapur, reportedly came to college wearing saffron shawls raising the slogan “Jai Shri Ram”. Meanwhile, the state government has asked institutions to follow existing uniform rules until the Karnataka High Court takes a call.advertisementOn Twitter, debates on the issue have raged on as well, a lot of them under the hashtag #KarnatakaHijabRow. Among these debates and opinions, however, were also images of women donning tricolour headscarves."If you have a dare to wear our Indian flag instead #HijabIsOurPride #HijabisOurRight #KarnatakaHijabRow," one such tweet read.Archived links of similar tweets can be seen here and here.India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) found the claim to be misleading. The photos in circulation with the claim that they are from Karnataka were actually taken at a Mumbai college during the Independence Day celebrations in 2018 and 2019.AFWA ProbeThe image in some of these tweets showed women marching, wearing tricolour hijab.A reverse search on Google took us to a report by the Financial Express published on August 15, 2018. The photo story was a collection of the best images of Independence Day celebrations from different parts of the country.The photo by the Press Trust of India (PTI) featured ninth in the story along with the caption, "Students of Anjuman Islam College march during the 72nd Independence Day parade, in Mumbai."Clearly, the image of college students in Mumbai was shared as a scene from Karnataka.We also checked the other image that is shared with similar claims. While the tweet claims the photo to be from Karnataka, a reverse search took us to an article by The Hindu published on December 30, 2019. It was a listicle of the most liked photos of the year on the daily’s Instagram page. The image in question was listed ninth in it along with the title, "Students of the Anjuman-I-Islam college in Mumbai don tricolour headscarves before flag hoisting during Independence Day celebrations at the college."We also located the photo on The Hindu's Instagram page. Uploaded on August 15, 2019, with the same caption, the photo was taken by the late senior photojournalist Vivek Bendre who died in 2021.Following the clue that the origin of both the images is the same, we ran a keyword search on Google for the Independence Day celebrations at Anjuman-I-Islam College. This returned several similar photos from 2019. One such image was also available on the website of the British-American visual media company Getty Images . It was captioned, “Students of Anjuman I Islam College take selfie to celebrate 73rd Independence Day, on August 15, 2019 in Mumbai, India.”A similar search on YouTube took us to a short video uploaded on August 15, 2020. We found students donning similar headscarves in this brief recap of the college's Independence Day celebration the previous year.Hence, it is clear that the images of women in tricolour headscarves shared with the claim that they are from Karnataka, were actually taken during Independence Day celebrations at Mumbai's Anjuman-I-Islam college. They have no connection with the ongoing hijab protests in the southern state.(With inputs from Yash Mittal in New Delhi)
label: truth

content: Fact Check: 50% seats in NIT-Goa reserved for home students, is it an exception?  As assembly polls approach Goa, a claim, supporting the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party, has gone viral on social media.Highlighting the achievements of the BJP government in Goa, a few social media users have stated that, “BJP has delivered 40% Reservations for Goans in NIT-Goa. It’s a special exception only for Goa.”India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) found that the viral claim was misleading. While it is true that 40 percent of seats in NIT Goa are reserved for “home students,” it is, however, no exception.advertisementAll NITs across the country have seat reservations under Home State Quota as prescribed by the Union Ministry of Education (formerly the Ministry of Human Resource Development).AFWA PROBEReservation in NIT-GoaWhile investigating the claim, we first conducted a keyword search to check if any such reservation exists in NIT-Goa.We found a news report published in May 2017. It stated that until 2016-17, NIT-Goa had a 50 percent reservation for Home State Quota, and that it was jointly shared by Goa along with Dadra Nagar Haveli, Diu and Daman and Lakshadweep.However, following a demand raised by former chief minister Manohar Parikkar, the criteria was changed. Starting with the 2017-18 session, 40 percent of seats would be reserved exclusively for the students of Goa, and the remaining ten percent would be shared by students from Dadra Nagar Haveli, Diu and Daman, and Lakshadweep.We then visited the website of Joint Seat Allocation Authority (JOSAA) to verify the current status of this allocation. Every year, the Ministry of Education sets up JOSAA to manage and regulate the joint seat allocation for admissions to 114 institutes for that academic year.The business rule formulated by JOSAA for the 2021-22 academic year states that NIT-Goa has a reservation of 50 percent seats for the Home State Quota.It stated that 40 percent of the Home State seats were reserved for students belonging to Goa. The remaining ten percent of the Home State seats are shared by students of Union Territories of Daman and Diu, Dadra Nagar Haveli, and Lakshadweep. However, any vacant Home State seats out of the ten percent mentioned above will be allocated to students from Goa.Reservation for other NITsThe business rule formulated by JOSAA clearly speaks of Home State seat reservation for other NITs as well.It states that apart from NIT-Goa and NIT-Srinagar, all NITs in India have 50 percent reservation for Home State Quota.Like NIT-Goa, NIT-Srinagar also has reservation for more than one state or union territories. A special quota of five percent seats in NIT-Srinagar are reserved for students of Ladakh. Any unfilled seats out of the five percent mentioned above can be filled by the students of Jammu and Kashmir.advertisementStudents of states or union territories where there are no NITs, can apply for the Home State Quota at other NITs as specified by JOSAA. However, unlike Goa and Srinagar, there is no limit for such reservations.To further confirm the rule, we got in touch with Dr. Kiran Teeparthi, the associate dean of NIT-Andhra Pradesh.“Every NIT in India has a 50 percent reservation for home students. Even we have it for NIT-Andhra Pradesh,” Teeparthi, who is an alumnus of NIT-Jamshedpur and NIT-Warangal, told India Today.What does “home state” mean?According to the JOSAA, eligible candidates who can apply for Home State quota are those candidates “whose Home State is the same as the state in which the Institute is located”.To understand the meaning of the criteria, we got in touch with Sumit Kumar Biswas, the Senior Superintendent of NIT-Durgapur.He explained that Home State Quota does not actually mean the state where the student’s permanent address is located. It is the registered address of the institution from where the student had appeared for their senior secondary exams.advertisement“Say, if a student from Nagaland had studied plus two from an institution in Bengal, then he would apply at NIT-Durgapur and not at NIT-Nagaland for Home State Quota,” Biswas explained.Hence, we can conclude that the viral claim is misleading. Not just NIT-Goa, every NIT in India has seats reserved under Home State Quota.
label: truth

content: Fact Check Video: SRK didn't spit while offering prayers for Lata Mangeshkar Prime Minister Narendra Modi attended the Christmas morning service at the Cathedral Church of the Redemption in New Delhi, joining a large congregation for prayers and carols. During the service, the Bishop of Delhi, Church of North India, Paul Swarup, led a special prayer for the Prime Minister, asking for wisdom and strength. Speaking to India Today, Bishop Swarup emphasised that Christmas is primarily a 'message of peace and joy and reconciliation,' which is crucial in a world facing disturbance and wars. He noted that while the Prime Minister did not speak, he participated in the liturgy to pray for the nation. The report also highlights PM Modi's regular engagement with the Christian community, including his attendance at a dinner at Minister George Kurian's residence in 2024.
label: rumor

content: Fact Check: Old image of BJP flags abandoned in waste container goes viral ahead of UP polls With only days away from the first phase of the Uttar Pradesh assembly polls, social media has been abuzz with heated campaigning by political parties, and a whole lot of misinformation spread by people, either knowingly or unwittingly.One such piece of misinformation was an image showing several Bharatiya Janata Party flags dumped in a public waste container, with the claim that this photo was from western Uttar Pradesh.advertisementRetired IAS officer Surya Pratap Singh was among the many who tweeted the picture. "Here, someone from western Uttar Pradesh sent this to me. Now, it’s up to you," the translation of the tweet from his verified handle read.India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) found the claim misleading. This photo has been in circulation for over three years at least.AFWA ProbeA reverse search of the image produced several results. Among them was a tweet from December 4, 2018.This confirmed that the image was definitely not a recent one and was at least three years old.More posts with the same photo were found on Facebook when we searched with the Hindi lines used in the tweet.We found that this image was used by supporters of different opposition parties to call out the BJP. Here is a tweet from 2021 using the same photo.We also found a photo story carried by lokmat.com on December 11, 2018, which contained the photo in question.The story was a compilation of top social media memes following the counting of assembly poll votes in five states on December 11. Telangana, Rajasthan, Chhattisgarh, Mizoram and Madhya Pradesh were the five states that witnessed the counting of votes on the day.Though the actual origin of the image couldn't be located, it is clear that the virally shared photo is not a recent one from poll-bound Uttar Pradesh.(With inputs from Sanjana Saxena in Lucknow)
label: truth

content: Fact Check: No, Shah Rukh Khan did not spit while offering prayers for Lata Mangeshkar A video clip of actor Shah Rukh Khan offering prayers for Lata Mangeshkar has gone viral for the wrong reasons. Many on social media shared this video, claiming that Khan spat after reciting prayers.Bharatiya Janata Party spokesperson Prashant Patel Umrao quote-tweeted another person who shared the viral video and wrote, “Shahrukh is Spitting!”.Another user posted the same video and wrote in the caption, “ Spitting while Paying last respects??? What an ugly culture @iamsrk !!! disrespectful to #LataDidi”.advertisementIndia Today Anti-Fake News War room (AFWA) found this misleading. Khan did not spit, rather he blew air after offering prayers. Reciting holy verses and then blowing air is called Ruqyah in Islamic tradition.The archived versions of the viral posts are saved here and here.Did SRK spit?After this claim was made by several people, many on social media shared the original video of the incident. While the viral video is only 13 seconds long, the longer version of the video shared online showed how the actor encircled the mortal remains of Lata Mangeshkar and made gestures to pay tribute to her. He was accompanied by his manager Pooja Dadlani.This was also reported by the mainstream media which can be seen here and here.To defend the actor’s gesture, some netizens even shared a clip from Khan’s film “My Name is Khan”, where he can be seen blowing air on his son in the movie.Scholars SpeakAFWA showed the viral video to a few Muslim scholars who are experts in Islamic studies.Professor Junaid Haris of the department of Islamic studies from Delhi’s Jamia Millia Islamia (JMI) university explained Khan’s gestures.“He is surely not spitting. This is a typical Muslim tradition of blowing air into something after reciting the holy verses. This is called Ruqyah or Ar-Ruqyah AshShar'iyyah in Arabic and Dum in Urdu,” said Professor Junaid Haris of JMI. “But I failed to understand why the actor is doing this in front of the mortal remains of somebody. This is not done during the last rites at all,” the professor added.We have found the definition of “Ruqyah” on Islamic websites that have elaborated on how to perform Ruqyah on old and sick persons.Muslims differ on whether Ruqyah can be performed for the dead.As per Asad Khan Falahi, another expert on Islamic studies told AFWA, “We normally perform this ritual of reciting Ayat and then performing Dum or blowing air on persons who are unwell and need blessings of Allah to be cured.”advertisement“You blow on something after reciting the holy verse, not on air. So, it could be Shah Rukh’s own belief that he has done during the last rites. But in Islam you do not do Ruqyiah in front of dead,” explained Haris.Islamic scholars might differ on the opinion of whether this Islamic ritual can be done on dead or not, but one thing is clear: Khan did not spit in front of Lata Mangeshkar’s mortal remains; rather he blew air following a Muslim tradition after offering prayers.
label: truth

content: Fact Check: Old hoax claiming Lata Mangeshkar sang ‘Yeh Jeevan Hai’ for Kishore Kumar resurfaces As India mourned the death of Lata Mangeshkar, tributes for the legendary singer poured in from all quarters on social media. Amid this, several netizens shared an emotional story involving Mangeshkar and another legendary singer, Kishore Kumar.The viral story claims that Lata Mangeshkar sang Kishore Kumar’s popular number ‘Yeh Jeevan Hai’ and gifted it to him on a special tape on her birthday.advertisementMultiple Facebook users have posted this story with the song of Lata Mangeshkar.The viral story read “Once Kishore Kumar asked Lata Mangeshkar, which of his song she liked the best. Lata smiled and asked him,’Dada, bol doon ya gaa kar sunao’... To which Kishore Da said, ‘Gaa kar hi sunaiye’. Lata laughed and said OK, but not today.”The story further read, “Few months later it was Lataji's birthday and Kishore Kumar received a gift box from Lataji. Kishore Da used to always wish Lataji on her birthday with gifts. It had a note on it from Lataji, it said, ‘Dada, aapne itni baar mere janamdin par tohfe bheje hain, ese return gift samaj lena, aur zaroor bataana aap ko agar aacha laga’. He opened the box and there was a tape inside.”The story also claimed, “It was the song Lataji loved most from all of Kishore Da's song... sung by Lata herself. She had contacted HMV recording studio and gone there recorded it only for Kishore Kumar. It seems Kishore Da listened to this song many times when he sat alone in his room. Nobody had heard this Kishore song sung by Lata exclusively for Kishore Kumar. Just listen to it, released by his wife Leena for the first time ever. Never heard before, enjoy.”India Today Anti-Fake News War Room (AFWA) found that the rendition of Kumar’s “Yeh Jeevan Hai” by Mangeshkar was not a private recording, especially for Kumar. It was part of Mangeshkar’s album “Shraddhanjali: My Tribute To The Immortals” where she paid a tribute to her colleagues from the singing world. Kumar’s “Yeh Jeevan Hai” from the film “Piya Ka Ghar” was one among them.The archived versions of the viral posts are saved here and here.AFWA probeWith the help of keywords search we found that this internet story has gone viral previously as well.We have found an article written by film critic Subhash K Jha and published last February last year on the portal IWMBUZZ.com. As per the report, the viral story is a hoax. The portal quoted Lata Mangeshkar, who denied the viral claim to the author.advertisement“I don’t recall any such incident. Kishore Da and I were very close to one another. He would make me laugh so much during our recordings for me. I cannot single out any one of his songs as my favourite. There were so many: Koi Lauta De Mere Beete Huey Din (from the film ‘Do Dooni Chaar’), Woh Sham Kuch Ajeeb Tthi (‘Khamoshi’), and Mera Jeevan Kora Kagaz (‘Kora Kagaz’). Kishoreda was filled with masti but when he sang, he projected so much emotion in his voice,” Mangeshkar had said at the time.Since the story went viral again after the passing of Lata Mangeshkar on Sunday, AFWA contacted the founder editor of the website IWMBUZZ.com, Siddhartha Laik to confirm the year-old story. “We stand by our story” , said Laik.To further cross check the viral story involving Lata Mangeshkar and Kishore Kumar, we contacted Mahesh Rathore, the private secretary to Lata Mangeshkar. “I have been with Lataji for the last 26 years. I have never heard this story from her or anybody else. This is probably the first time I am hearing this”, Rathore told AFWA over the phone.advertisementAFWA contacted writer, poet Yatindra Mishra, the author of the award-winning book, "Lata- Sur Gatha" — a biography in Hindi on Mangeshkar published in 2016. “ I have never heard about any such incident from Lataji ever,” Mishra told us.The song “Yeh Jeevan Hai” was composed by Laxmikant-Pyarelal for the film “Piya Ka Ghar.” Mangeshkar’s cover of the song can be found on a number of music-streaming platforms like Gaana and JioSaavn.Thus, we conclude that the viral story involving Lata Mangeshkar and Kishore Kumar and the song “Yeh Jeevan Hai” is a baseless rumour.READ: Fact Check: Youth from Bihar didn't hack into Google, nor was he offered Rs 3.66 cr jobALSO READ: Fact Check: No, this photo is not from 'inaugural' Air India flight after Tata takeover
label: truth

content: Fact Check: Year-old Defence Ministry report shared with dynasty spin ahead of UP polls Unemployment is one of the foremost issues in the upcoming Assembly polls in Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, Uttarakhand, Manipur, and Goa. Parties contesting for the polls have therefore made jobs-creation an important plank. On social media, however, an image has gone viral that shows a newspaper report about the Defence Ministry abolishing 9,300 posts.A viral screenshot of the newspaper report also carried an image of Defence Minister Rajnath Singh. The headline of the report in Hindi reads, “9,300 Military Engineer Services posts abolished by the Defence Ministry."advertisementSharing the cut-out of this report, several Facebook users called Singh out. For example, one user shared this screenshot alongside a caption quoting, “Both his sons got tickets for the 2022 assembly elections. That's why the job ticket for our children has been cancelled.”Archived versions of similar claims can be seen here and here.India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) found this claim to be misleading as only one of Rajnath Singh’s sons has been given a ticket for the upcoming polls. At the same time, the news report in the photo is also an old one.AFWA ProbeWith the help of some keywords, we found Rajnath Singh’s family details in a Jagran Josh report. It mentioned that the former Home Minister has two sons and a daughter named Pankaj Singh, Neeraj Singh, and Anamika Singh respectively.After searching for keywords of Pankaj Singh, it led us to an Economic Times report which noted that he is already the sitting MLA from Noida, and has now been awarded a ticket for the second time from the same constituency by the Bharatiya Janata Party.But when we searched for the keywords of Neeraj Singh, no such result appeared, which could suggest that he had been given a ticket too. A National Herald report stated that Neeraj has been denied a ticket by the party. It also mentioned that this time, the BJP decided to not give tickets to family members of elected representatives, barring those who are already elected members.Further, a Fact-Check story by the “Viswas News” made it clear that Rajnath’s younger son Neeraj Singh, hasn’t got a ticket from the party.While looking closely into the viral newspaper cutting, we noticed that “Jagran Bureau” was written below the headline. After searching for keywords related to this, it took us to a Jagran report published on May 7, 2020. Media outlets like the Hindustan Times and The Indian Express also published similar reports on May 7 and 8, 2020. The abolition of the posts, reportedly, is one of the outcomes of recommendations made by the Lt Gen DB Shekatkar committee report on enhancing the army’s combat potential and trimming its expenditure.Therefore, we conclude that the claim made in the viral post is misleading as one, this is an old news report, and two, not both of Rajnath Singh’s sons have gotten a ticket for the upcoming polls.(With inputs from Riddhish Dutta)READ: Fact Check: Old video from Darjeeling passed off as BJP leader being heckled in UPALSO READ: Fact Check: Video of UP election candidate saying he wants to ‘earn money by becoming MLA’ is from 2017
label: truth

content: Fact Check: Youth from Bihar didn't hack into Google, nor was he offered Rs 3.66 cr job Stories of white hat hackers getting job offers from tech giants after bringing said giants down to their knees through their mysterious hacking skills are fun to hear or read. They echo themes of David and Goliath that many enjoy. But a lot of times, the story is not what you hear. Such is the case of a young man from Bihar, whose exploits are being mythologised online.advertisementMany on social media shared an image of a young man called Rituraj Chaudhary who did something extraordinary: he hacked the world’s largest search engine website, Google, in a matter of seconds.The viral post in Hindi roughly translates to, “This man, Rituraj Chaudhary, hacked Google for 51 seconds a few nights ago. Google officials in the USA went crazy. But Rituraj resumed Google’s services and mailed them about a flaw on their website that can be used to hack the system.”This claim further adds, “Google held a meeting for 12 hours in the US and finally decided to hire Rituraj and sent him an offer letter with a package of Rs 3.66 crores per annum. Rituraj didn’t have a passport. So, Google talked to the Government of India, and the newly made passport reached his home within two hours. Rituraj will fly to the US in a private jet. He is studying B.Tech second-year in IIT Manipur and belongs to Mungergunj, a small village near Bihar’s Begusarai.”Archived versions of similar claims can be found here and here.India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) found these viral posts to be misleading. Rituraj didn’t hack Google but found a security bug in their website. He is neither going to the USA nor is he joining Google.AFWA ProbeUsing keywords, we searched the Internet for news reports on this and came across an article published by DNA on February 4.In that report stated no extraordinary tale, just that Chaudhary informed Google about a flaw or bug in the website that could have easily helped hackers’ to take advantage.According to a report published in Dainik Bhaskar on February 3, Google admitted to the flaw at their end and sent Chaudhary an acknowledgement mail. The report further added that Google often rewards those who find flaws on their website. Currently, Chaudhary’s findings were in the Phase-2 level. He will be awarded by Google when they reach Phase-0.Many researchers work on “bug hunt” for Google, which starts at Phase-5 and goes up to Phase-0.An AajTak report confirmed that Chaudhary’s name was included in the researchers' list of Google. We dug further on this and found the list of bug hunters by Google where Chaudhary’s name was featured.While speaking to The Lallantop, Chaudhary dismissed rumours about getting a job in Google worth Rs 3.66 crores and flying to the USA. Chaudhary also added that he was not an IIT-Manipur student — there is no IIT in Manipur. He is, in fact, a student at the Indian Institute of Information Technology Manipur (IIIT-Manipur).When AFWA reached out to Chaudhary, he texted back saying, “All the rumours about getting a job in Google and flying to the states are fake. It is impossible to make a passport within hours.” When asked about receiving a reward from Google, he said, “Google gives rewards after they fix that bug and that takes around two to three months.”Therefore, we conclude that the stories about Chaudhary joining Google and receiving a huge salary are not true.(with inputs from Riddhish Dutta)
label: truth

content: Fact Check: Old video shared as Baloch fighters shooting down Pak military chopper Pakistani troops clashed with the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) following two attacks by the insurgent group. While the BLA claimed hundreds of Pakistani defence personnel were killed in the attacks on army posts in Naushki and Panjgur districts, the Pakistani government claimed that the final death toll stands at 20 militants and nine soldiers.A video was shared on social media claiming that it captured the terrorist organisation shooting down a Pakistani military helicopter in Panjgur. "#Balochistan Exclusive footage of Pak Army helicopter shot down by Balochistan libration Armyfreedom fighters in #Panjgur," one such tweet claimed.advertisementIndia Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) found the claim to be misleading. The video used in the tweet was shared online at least as early as 2020.AFWA ProbeThe video was of poor quality and was too pixelated to run a keyframe search. But we found a better version of the same video posted as a reply to the tweet by a user who alleged the claim to be wrong.Posted on November 9, 2020, the tweet read, “Nagorno-Karabakh: Russian helicopter shot down over Armenia. Azerbaijan has admitted to shooting the aircraft down by accident."We ran a reverse search of the video's keyframes on Yandex and found several posts dating back to November 2020. Most of these were posted by Russian users that claimed what the video showed was a Russian chopper shot down by Azerbaijan.The video was uploaded on November 10, 2020, on Instagram by “chp.kbr” — a local news page that appears to be from Russia's Nalchik region. "The Azerbaijani Foreign Ministry said that the country's army accidentally shot down a Russian helicopter and apologizes to the Russian side," the English translation of the Russian caption read.A similar claim was found on another Russian Instagram page called “armiya_rf” that uploaded the video on November 9, 2020. "These frames appeared on the network, eyewitnesses claim that they captured the moment the missile hit the Russian Mi-24," the post on the page with more than 200,000 followers said.The video was also found published on an independent news website called “bulgarianmilitary.com” with the same claim on November 10, 2020.We ran a Google keyword search to find out more about the circumstances that led to the incident. Long-standing rivals Armenia and Azerbaijan fought over the control of the Nagorno-Karabakh region for over a month starting in late September 2020. The conflict ended in a decisive Azerbaijani victory on November 10, 2020, who took control of the Armenian-dominated Nagorno-Karabakh.On November 9, 2020, a Russian Mi-24 military helicopter was mistakenly shot down by Azerbaijan while flying over Armenia. The ill-fated chopper was accompanying a column of Russian troops in Armenia while it was hit by the Azeri missile. Two of the crew died while another sustained injury, reports said. Azerbaijan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs released an apology and offered compensation following the incident.advertisementThe date of the incident matches the time when most of the Russian handles had published the video on social media. We found the same video on YouTube claiming to be of the shot down Mi-24.Though not the same one in question, a similar video was found in a report by the Daily Star on November 9, 2020, which showed the burning wreckage of the helicopter.It is thus clear that the video is not from the recent clashes in Balochistan.
label: truth

content: Fact Check: Viral video does not show Kanhaiya Kumar getting beaten up by Congress workers Just days away from the first phase of the Uttar Pradesh assembly polls, social media saw claims that Kanhaiya Kumar, Congress's new star recruit, was heckled and attacked by his own party member in Lucknow. Sharing a video of the alleged incident, some Facebook users claimed that Kanhaiya was beaten by his own party workers.The claim, originally in Hindi, roughly translates to, "Rahul Gandhi's darling Kanhaiya Kumar has been beaten by Congress workers." A flag of the Congress party is visible in the low-quality video.advertisementArchived versions of some similar posts can be seen here and here.India Today Anti Fake News War Room found this claim to be not true. Kumar was not being attacked in the video making the claim.AFWA ProbeWith the help of some keywords from the viral post, we came across a report published in "The Times of India" on February 2. It stated that "ink" was allegedly thrown at Kumar by a youth named Devansh Bajpai in the Lucknow Party office.But Kanhaiya Kumar was not seen in the viral video. It was still not clear who was the person being heckled in that viral video. So, with the help of the Invid tool, we took some screenshots of the viral video and ran a reverse image search.This led us to multiple media reports of that day about this incident in the Congress office. We came across a video uploaded by News24 on its YouTube channel on February 1 alongside a caption in Hindi which translates to, "Ink thrown on Kanhaiya Kumar outside the Congress party office." When we compared both frames, it became clear that both the videos are the same and this video is from the Lucknow party office of Congress.We found another video report published by Zee Uttar Pradesh-Uttarakhand where it was mentioned that Devansh Bajpai, who allegedly threw "chemicals" at Kanhaiya, was beaten by the party workers. But the suspect's face was not visible enough.Further search took us to a YouTube video uploaded by Times Now on February 1. In this video, the man Bajpai can easily be seen at the 11-12 second mark. His face reappears clearly towards the end of the video.So we conclude that the viral video claiming Kanhaiya Kumar has been beaten by his own party workers is not true. It was Devansh Bajpai who got heckled by Congress workers.(with inputs from Riddhish Dutta)
label: truth

content: Fact Check: Ajit Anjum did not tweet he will leave journalism if BJP comes back to power in UP The voters of Uttar Pradesh head to the polling booths for the first phase of Assembly elections in a few days. Social media is abuzz with heated campaigns by political parties. A lot of misinformation is also passed over these platforms as the voting day draw closer.In the latest, a tweet, purportedly by senior journalist Ajit Anjum is circulated on social media where he claims to leave journalism if BJP comes back to power in UP.advertisementIndia Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) has found that the tweet circulated as Ajit Anjum's is fake. The journalist himself told us that he has not made any such announcement on Twitter.AFWA probeAccording to the screenshot in circulation, Ajit Anjum made the tweet on January 31, 2022.We checked Ajit Anjum's tweets from his official handle (@ajitanjum) n this date but couldn't find it. We also checked the archived version of the tweet in question on the web archiving tool "Wayback Machine". However, none of the Tweets made by Ajit Anjum on January 31 or the adjacent days was available in the archives.Also, as per the screenshot, Ajit Anjum made the tweet from a verified Twitter handle. However, the official handle of Ajit Anjum -- which has over 1.2 million followers is not verified. Ajit's Twitter followers include several political leaders and journalists.For further clarity, we further reached out to Ajit Anjum. Speaking to AFWA, the journalist said, "A few days back some social media handles were claiming that I have announced to leave journalism if Yogi Adityanath comes back to power in UP. Now, a fake screenshot of a tweet is in circulation claiming that I will leave my profession if BJP comes back to power in UP. All these are absurd. I have never made any such remarks. Also, my Twitter handle @ajitanjum is not verified. However, the fake screenshot in circulation has a verification tick mark."On February 5, 2022, Ajit Anjum himself shared the screenshot of the alleged tweet and confirmed he never posted such a remark on the microblogging platform.On the same day, Ajit also tweeted a video of him speaking about the fake social media posts circulating in his name and the frequent trolls he receives from the IT cells.advertisementThe video is shared with a caption in Hindi that translates as, "Various types of false rumours are being spread about me in a planned manner. Photoshop creations are also circulated. It shows how much the IT cell dislikes me touring the country and voicing my opinion."It is hence clear that the screenshot circulated in the name of Ajit Anjum is fake. The journalist never tweeted saying he will leave journalism if BJP comes back to power in UP.(With inputs from Kamala Kuniyal in New Delhi)
label: truth

content: Fact Check: Old video from Darjeeling passed off as BJP leader being heckled in UP Amid the high-octane election campaign in Uttar Pradesh, a video showing BJP leaders getting heckled by people has gone viral with the claim that this happened in Uttar Pradesh recently.Multiple Facebook and Twitter users shared the video with the caption in Hindi that translates to, “The condition of BJP is pathetic. Another BJP leader was welcomed in Uttar Pradesh with kicks and punches.”advertisementIndia Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) has found that the viral video is from West Bengal. In 2017 Dilip Ghosh, the former state president of BJP and others were heckled and chased in Darjeeling by locals.These viral posts have been archived here and here.AFWA probeWith the help of the InVid tool and reverse image search we have found the truth behind the viral video. A similar video of the attack on the BJP leaders was uploaded on the YouTube channel of ABP News with the title “Attack on BJP President Dilip Ghosh in Darjeeling “. A similar video of the incident was also uploaded on another YouTube channel called NMF News. Both these videos were uploaded on October 6, 2017.According to these news clips, the now-BJP national vice president along with a few others were heckled by locals in Darjeeling. The incident was reported by The Indian Express on October 6, 2017.As per this report, after the withdrawal of the indefinite strike called by the Gorkha Janmukti Morcha (GJM) on the issue of Gorkhaland, a Bengal BJP delegation led by Dilip Ghosh, the former state president of the party, visited Darjeeling. As per the news report, Ghosh was chased and heckled, allegedly by supporters of Binay Tamang in Darjeeling.As per news reports, a couple of weeks ago during the Uttar Pradesh election campaign, BJP MLA Vikram Singh Saini was chased away by people in his constituency in Muzaffarnagar, Uttar Pradesh.But the viral video in question is a five-year-old one from Darjeeling, West Bengal, and has no link to the UP election.
label: rumor

content: Fact Check: Video of UP election candidate saying he wants to ‘earn money by becoming MLA’ is from 2017 Election is a time when politicians try to present their best selves in front of the electorate. But a video recently making the rounds on social media flies in the face of such conventional wisdom.The video in question sees a man openly confessing that he is contesting elections for money and personal gain. According to the social media posts, he is a candidate contesting for the upcoming Uttar Pradesh assembly elections. “I’m not contesting elections on any issue. I’m fighting for a personal agenda, which is to earn money by becoming an MLA,” the man can be heard saying in the video.advertisementThe archived versions of a similar post can be seen here.India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) has found that the claim along with the video is misleading. This video is from the 2017 assembly election in UP.AFWA probeThe video in question has the logo of the news website, The Quint. In the video, the man has been identified as an independent candidate Gopal Chaudhary and for a fraction of a second, ‘Agra’ can be seen written on the top-right corner of the video.We did a keyword search and found the same video report published by The Quint on January 28, 2017. This confirms that the video is old and is not related to the upcoming UP elections which will be held in seven phases from February 10 to March 10.The description of the video reads as follows, “The election season is upon us and from Prime Minister Narendra Modi to Congress Vice President Rahul Gandhi, everyone is busy making election promises to the voters. However, Gopal Chaudhary, one of the independent candidates from the Agra constituency, has a different approach. Chaudhary sent ripples across social media when he made an ‘honest claim’ that he is contesting elections to make money and he has no intention to work for public welfare.”Several media outlets also reported this unusual confession made by a candidate.According to a 2017 report in The Indian Express, Chaudhary contested the 2017 assembly elections in UP from the Agra South constituency. Chaudhary received 464 (0.21 per cent) votes in the election.The election to the 17th Uttar Pradesh Legislative Assembly was held from February 11 to March 8, 2017The viral video was also tweeted by ANI on January 27, 2017.#WATCH: Independent candidate Agra South Gopal Chaudhary says 'my only reason for coming into politics is money, I'll fool people" pic.twitter.com/sYfPIdhiYC — ANI UP/Uttarakhand (@ANINewsUP) January 27, 2017It is hence clear that the video in question is over five years old and not is related to the upcoming elections.
label: truth

content: Fact Check: Predecessor al-Baghdadi's photo shared as dead IS chief Abu Ibrahim al-Qurayshi On January 20, militants of the Islamic State attacked Ghwaryan prison, which reportedly housed more than 3,000 of their comrades. The attack triggered a retaliation. The international coalition-supported Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF) took 11 days to complete their counter-operation and regain control. The operation reportedly claimed the lives of 121 SDF personnel and four civilians along with that of 374 IS fighters.advertisementAbu Ibrahim al-Hashimi al-Qurayshi was killed during a raid by US forces on a house in northern Syria on Wednesday, February 2. Reportedly, al-Qurayshi, who was named the leader of ISIL shortly after his predecessor Abu Bakr al-Baghdadi's death in 2019, blew himself up during the raid, killing members of his own family.Following the announcement of his death, Twitter was abuzz with information on the Islamic State leader. Several people shared images of the raided building along with alleged images of al-Qurayshi. Among these is a close-up photo of a bearded middle-aged man donning a jacket and headscarf."Islamic State leader Abu Ibrahim al-Qurayshi killed in Syria -- US", one such tweet read.India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) has found the image to be misleading. The man in the picture is in fact al-Baghdadi -- al-Qurayshi's predecessor.AFWA ProbeAlso called Abdullah Qardash and Amir Mohammed Said Abdul Rahman al-Mawla, al-Qurayshi was with his family on the second floor of a three-storey residential building in Atmeh, Syria when the US forces struck. As per reports, US officials said the military chose to conduct a raid with troops instead of bombing the compound to minimise harm to the family that lived on the first floor.
